gates.protects: A verified engine patch upgrade must not discard an otherwise valid native session binding.
gates.baseline: Same-version and legacy-unbound resumes retain existing behavior; session, workspace, skill and first-message identity checks remain strict.
gates.failureFallback: Only the explicitly verified forward version pair is compatible. Unknown upgrades, downgrades and foreign or missing artifacts retain isolated fresh-session recovery.

gates.protects: Explicit upstream credential refresh rejection cannot be hidden inside retryable gateway errors or loop indefinitely.
gates.baseline: Ordinary transient provider failures retain bounded recovery and unrelated sessions remain unaffected.
gates.failureFallback: Surface confirmed session-owned non-retryable auth failures without replay; preserve distinction from Lily gateway credentials.

gates.protects: Damaged local history cannot silently become empty history or disable the independent recovery entry point.
gates.baseline: Healthy startup and new user tasks remain available; ordinary SQLite transaction recovery does not disable normal task continuity.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve original database and journals, require confirmation for older snapshots, bound repair workers and keep ambiguous outcomes visible without automatic replay.

gates.protects: Committed conversation articles retain chronological order across interleaved history and live updates.
gates.baseline: Existing article identity, detached reading and per-panel rendering remain available.
gates.failureFallback: Invalidate stale render jobs and rebuild the owning window without discarding committed messages.

gates.protects: Committed local history survives legacy migration and interrupted database compaction without silent empty-store replacement.
gates.baseline: Healthy stores, existing history merging and WAL compaction refusal remain available; diagnostics do not mutate customer data.
gates.failureFallback: Keep source databases, backups and journals on ambiguity or I/O failure; retry migration later, refuse destructive replacement and report the actual error category.

gates.protects: Task verification and durable completion cannot hide outstanding work or invent successful checks.
gates.baseline: Answers remain deliverable without machine-verifiable evidence; existing bounded engine and parent recovery remain available.
gates.failureFallback: Unknown, stale, failed or incomplete evidence remains unverified or observed. Automatic continuation requires durable shared limits and never bypasses user input or cancellation.

gates.protects: Collaboration dialogs and detail surfaces remain visible, actionable, and isolated from stale asynchronous results.
gates.baseline: Creation drafts and focus survive locale and directory refreshes; confirmations, retries, and navigation remain usable in narrow and dark layouts.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve drafts and original command identities, show actionable failures, and ignore late results after a surface is closed or replaced.

gates.protects: Optional collaboration cannot break AI work, cross accounts, fabricate delivery, lose cached history, or expose unverified decrypted files.
gates.baseline: AI workbench behavior remains unchanged when collaboration is disabled or unavailable; collaboration uses its own encrypted store.
gates.failureFallback: Disable the optional service on initialization failure, retain original durable command identities on ambiguous delivery, fence stopped instances, and reject unauthorized or corrupted data.

gates.protects: Unsent message edits cannot leak plaintext, cross accounts, lose newer window state, or survive access revocation.
gates.baseline: Composer drafts remain unchanged while edit drafts use a separate encrypted account/conversation/message record.
gates.failureFallback: Reject malformed or stale generations, fence stopped/replaced services, and delete edit drafts transactionally on revocation.

gates.protects: Collaboration cannot replace or crush the primary workbench, start open unexpectedly, or regress to the legacy three-column canvas.
gates.baseline: The AI workbench remains fully visible and Collaboration is available from a separate default-collapsed right-side entry.
gates.failureFallback: Keep the panel closed with zero reserved width and preserve the ordinary workbench when collaboration presentation is unavailable.

gates.protects: Local task classification and verification cannot be disabled by remote configuration.
gates.baseline: The bundled deterministic task registry remains active.
gates.failureFallback: Ignore malformed, disabled, or unsupported remote overlays and use the local baseline.

gates.protects: Retry, rescue, evidence, and TaskRun code agree about side effects and replay safety.
gates.baseline: Unknown tools and shell commands are never replayed automatically.
gates.failureFallback: Treat unknown semantics as external-side-effectful and not replay-safe.

gates.protects: Durable user intent is resolved before capability preparation and dispatch.
gates.baseline: Current-turn deterministic classification uses the original selected model, tools, context, and user text.
gates.failureFallback: Planner or continuity errors return the current-turn baseline without blocking dispatch.

gates.protects: Main, persistence, and renderer share versioned RuntimeEvent and TaskRun contracts.
gates.baseline: Existing event names and TaskRun fields stay compatible.
gates.failureFallback: Reject unsupported versions and malformed typed producer payloads before persistence or rendering.

gates.protects: Workspace version protection remains available to ordinary customers without a manual Git installation and does not regress on large Git-backed workspaces.
gates.baseline: Missing Git or a failed dependency install falls back to the existing local snapshot backend without deleting user files.
gates.failureFallback: Resolve the hidden Git runtime pack first, then system Git; if both are unavailable, keep the local snapshot path and surface the existing coded save error for files beyond its documented bounds.

gates.protects: Internal prompt layers cannot crowd out the original user request.
gates.baseline: Normal-size prompt layers and the full visible user message remain byte-identical.
gates.failureFallback: Bound only oversized internal layers and preserve explicit truncation diagnostics.

gates.protects: External factual claims in known or previously unseen domains cannot be asserted from model memory alone, and the evidence gate cannot make the platform dumber by erasing supported content.
gates.baseline: External fact requests are risk-tiered (hard / verify_soft / advisory) and model-first: only high-stakes asks (the medical/legal/finance floor, or the turn judge's stakes=high verdict) fail closed; ordinary asks auto-verify once and on final failure keep a BOUNDED answer (supported subset or original under a verification banner) — delivered content never drops to zero while any supported content exists. Semantic judgments (support, authority, conflicts, informal labels) belong to one unified judge call per turn, never to domain regex vocabularies; the deterministic layer keeps the literal floor (URL/entity/number grounding, ledger counts) and fabricated entities are never banner-kept. Protection vocabulary covers zh/en/ar equally.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_EVIDENCE_RISK_TIERS=0 restores exact legacy all-hard behavior. Internal gate errors fail closed only on the hard tier; verify_soft/advisory fail open with the original answer. Malformed semantic plans or recovery context preserve the existing strict host gate. A single changed-strategy retry may inherit only bounded successful read-only external evidence from the immediately completed turn; internal retry prompts stay hidden and durable supersession prevents pre-gate engine text from returning on history reload. Otherwise disclose the limit without fabricating an answer.

gates.protects: Image and document reading requests cannot be routed as generation or answered without readable source content. A partially-read attachment is READ rather than apologised for: the shortfall the ledger already detects now has a recovery round, the same one-shot route every other detected shortfall uses.
gates.baseline: The platform resolves operation, source kind, and expected output before routing, then records source coverage separately from tool activity. A PARTIAL read no longer erases the answer. Bytes were read, and evidence-gate says so itself — it reports hasEvidence: true and fails only when the answer does not disclose the partial scope — so the analysis of what was read stands and the missing sentence is appended, with how much was observed. The decision is three-way: nothing read is replaced (any content claim is fabricated by construction), an answer claiming to cover the whole source while only part was read is replaced (a false statement about pages nobody saw), and an honestly partial answer is kept with its scope disclosed in wording the gate itself accepts as a disclosure.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve the original attachment and strong model path, disclose the read failure, and replace unsupported source claims before projection.

gates.protects: User edits to a generated or attached file cannot be overwritten from stale attachment snapshots, knowledge-index excerpts, or historical write/edit tool inputs.
gates.baseline: The readable live filesystem path is authoritative; unchanged history remains available and missing live files retain their recoverable historical content.
gates.failureFallback: Use the staged copy only when the original is unavailable, drop fingerprint-mismatched index hits, and require a successful live read before modifying an existing changed file. A refusal always names a tool that satisfies it and says which ways do not, because a guard that cannot be satisfied is worse than no guard: the field case was an agent refused an edit to a file it had just read, falling back to rewriting it from a script — the unchecked write this gate exists to prevent. What counts as having read a file mirrors the platform's own classification (evidenceKind file_read) instead of a second, narrower list.

gates.protects: Delivered output is not presented as verified completion without required evidence.
gates.baseline: Legacy status remains compatible while completionStatus records verification truth.
gates.failureFallback: Use delivered_unverified or observed_work instead of verified_complete.

gates.protects: A persisted empty assistant turn cannot poison every later model call and prevent tools or compaction from running.
gates.baseline: Healthy text history and tool-call/result protocol messages remain byte-identical and in their original order.
gates.failureFallback: Add one bounded neutral text marker only to truly provider-empty assistant messages; plugin errors and the kill switch retain baseline behavior.

gates.protects: Generated or edited Office and PDF files cannot be presented as polished verified deliverables without an actual output, deterministic structure checks, rendering, and visual inspection.
gates.baseline: Bundled Python authoring remains available for Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF, with managed LibreOffice rendering and CJK-safe font discovery.
gates.failureFallback: Preserve the generated file and label it delivered_unverified; run at most one path-scoped QA continuation, then disclose any remaining verification gap without replaying the authoring task.

gates.protects: Critical modules do not grow new mixed responsibilities or cross process boundaries.
gates.baseline: Existing hotspots may be split and reduced but not enlarged.
gates.failureFallback: The architecture test fails before a capability change can merge.

gates.protects: A user's first upward wheel or touch gesture cannot be overwritten by queued live-render auto-follow callbacks.
gates.baseline: The active conversation follows new output while the user remains at the latest message, and explicit Latest navigation re-enables following.
gates.failureFallback: Cancel stale scheduled auto-follow after any newer navigation intent, preserve the user's reading position, and keep explicit force-to-latest available.

gates.protects: Character card parsing, session binding, or context compilation changes a native turn, crosses conversations, displaces Lily guidance, exposes private card data, or lets imported executable behavior run.
gates.baseline: Native conversations send byte-equivalent Lily/OpenCode prompt bodies with no card parsing or extra model request; character bindings are local, optional, immutable-revision pinned, conversation-scoped, owner-scoped, and snapshotted in the admission transaction; character context is a bounded lower-authority system suffix after the protected Lily prefix.
gates.failureFallback: Disabled, missing, corrupt, oversized, or hostile cards, bindings, revisions, macros, compilation, budgets, and providers without safe system context fail open to the byte-identical native turn with exactly one dispatch; a missing, corrupt, resolver-failing, or over-budget world book never breaks a bound character turn — the character compiles to the byte-identical no-book body (§16) and read-only book inspection stays available; a missing, corrupt, or over-budget persona revision never breaks a bound character turn either — the character+book compiles to the byte-identical no-persona body; authoring edits create new immutable revisions and never alter an already-admitted turn's pinned snapshot or compiled body (update-available requires an explicit apply); retries, recovery, queue promotion, and steer inherit by trusted source turn id instead of rereading the binding; the LILY_CHARACTER_WORLDS=0 kill switch and signed rollout policy restore native behavior without touching stored data; imported scripts, plugins, regex scripts, and unknown macros never execute; an agent draft (tool disabled, kill switch, hostile or over-cap draft input, missing authoring service, malformed injected context block) fails closed to a coded error with NO durable write and the native turn stays byte-equivalent; a workspace pack import with a missing referenced revision or hostile character-worlds section degrades to a native conversation + diagnostic and never leaves a half-imported library (entities import only through validated writers with canonical-hash dedup; bindings restore only when their referenced revisions imported).

gates.protects: A selected character must reach the final model request as an active conversational identity without changing Lily's tools, permissions, safety, evidence, task rigor, exact technical content, or requested output format.
gates.baseline: Native conversations remain byte-identical; selected roles use a host-owned fingerprint-bound activation layer after the protected Lily kernel and a separately delimited lower-authority narrative envelope.
gates.failureFallback: Invalid, unsupported, compile-failed, or over-budget role layers run native Lily and emit metadata-only bypass evidence; only a final-boundary applied receipt scoped to the current session, turn, and immutable revision may render as active.

gates.protects: Character preview actions remain clickable and recover visibly when activation or exit fails.
gates.baseline: The preview banner stays above the active conversation hit-testing layer and reserves message space.
gates.failureFallback: Keep the current preview active, clear busy state, refresh preview state, and show a retryable error instead of leaving a dead control.

gates.protects: AI character, persona, and world-book creation cannot report ordinary files as persisted library entities or trust editable official tags.
gates.baseline: Non-authoring requests retain native Lily behavior; authoring succeeds only after validated immutable library persistence.
gates.failureFallback: Retry failed persistence twice, then explicitly report not saved; preserve the requirement through durable queues and never bind automatically.

gates.protects: A shared engine or broker cannot borrow another conversation's identity, capabilities, workspace, or authority.
gates.baseline: Each broker call is authorized from a signed, expiring, request-scoped host identity.
gates.failureFallback: Reject missing or invalid grants without weakening the native non-broker turn path.

gates.protects: Concurrent agents cannot double-claim work, unlock dependencies early, or cross session mailbox boundaries.
gates.baseline: Task graphs use durable revisioned claims, leases, dependency state, and replay-safe retry policy.
gates.failureFallback: Disable task-graph projection and preserve the existing single-agent TaskRun path.

gates.protects: Partial or corrupt checkpoints cannot be restored and irreversible effects cannot be silently replayed.
gates.baseline: Committed checkpoint manifests are integrity-checked, idempotent, scoped, and preserve fork lineage.
gates.failureFallback: Keep the existing OpenCode revert and in-memory diff behavior when unified checkpoints are disabled.

gates.protects: Headless clients cannot depend on renderer internals or an unstable event stream.
gates.baseline: Legacy JSON remains compatible while versioned NDJSON and SDK contracts are additive.
gates.failureFallback: Use the legacy headless JSON path with stable non-zero exit codes.

gates.protects: Public hooks cannot recurse, leak secrets, hang turns, or mutate protected identity and authority.
gates.baseline: Hooks are schema, timeout, recursion, audit, and mutation bounded.
gates.failureFallback: Observation failures fail open, security denials fail closed, and the hook kill switch bypasses hooks.

gates.protects: Auto/manual choices cannot cross conversations, widen custom pools, lose retry identity, conflate providers, bypass the quality floor for vision, or drift between execution, compaction and usage models.
gates.baseline: Recommended Auto preserves the active model when reliable metadata is absent; per-turn execution profiles drive main/helper models and budgets while retaining bulk-input staging and history compaction.
gates.failureFallback: Recommended Auto can use the legacy active engine only when the catalog is unavailable, not when models are revoked. Expired catalogs refresh once. Ambiguous legacy identities and explicit choices never silently change models.

gates.protects: Packaged Lily can discover installed local command-line software without inheriting unrelated host secrets or unsafe search paths.
gates.baseline: Bundled runtimes and verified packs keep priority while existing absolute platform, installer, inherited, and login-shell executable directories remain discoverable.
gates.failureFallback: Ignore failed login-shell discovery and continue with the bounded known system and installer paths.

gates.protects: A long task that finished is reported as finished: the unfinished-todo gate cannot push a blocked model back into the same turn indefinitely, and a turn that produced a real answer is never labelled stalled or contradicted by a 'no final answer' banner. The deliverable completion gate judges only STRUCTURED evidence — deliverables the task contract declares and files this turn's own file-writing tool calls produced (turn-artifacts.producedPathFromTool) — never paths read out of the answer prose, as Claude Code and Codex CLI ground 'what was produced' in the tool ledger. When the gate does fire, its corrective round is appended to the user's answer instead of replacing it.
gates.baseline: A model that quits with work genuinely left is still nudged to continue, and a turn that produced no answer at all still gets the stalled terminal with its salvageable tool results. 2026-09-28: a how-to answer ('装好后编辑配置 `/etc/shadowsocks-rust/config.json`' on the user's server) was gated as a missing local deliverable by a prose-path regex; the model was pushed to write a real password config into the repo and the corrective round's 'file now exists' replaced the proxy answer the user asked for.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_DISABLE_TODO_COMPLETION_GATE=1 disables the gate entirely; a snapshot without todos skips it, and the summary builder degrades to plain assistant text. Mutation-verified 2026-09-28: re-reading prose paths as claims, not recording the tool ledger, and letting the corrective round replace the answer each fail test-opencode-agent-session by name.

gates.protects: A cleanly ended turn cannot be re-entered by completion gates round after round: every gate that pushes a finished turn back into the model draws on one shared per-turn budget.
gates.baseline: Each gate keeps its own no-progress logic and still gets to correct a genuinely unfinished turn; the required-tool persistence check still fails loudly instead of passing silently.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_TURN_CONTINUATION_BUDGET=0 removes the shared cap and restores per-gate-only bounds; malformed overrides fail open to the default and a missing gate state never blocks a turn.

gates.protects: Time a turn spends blocked on the user (a permission or question card) is attributed to the user, never reported as the assistant's own latency, and the progress heartbeat names waiting as waiting instead of claiming to be working.
gates.baseline: Ordinary tools still show their real elapsed compute time, and the heartbeat still reports genuine tool progress once no card is open.
gates.failureFallback: A missed begin/end hook, absent/negative/oversized waitMs, or a missing translate all degrade to today's plain elapsed time; wait time is never shown as compute.

gates.protects: Compacting a runtime event for persistence bounds its size without erasing the fields a human or a replay needs — notably the option labels of a question card.
gates.baseline: The depth cap still bounds payload size: nesting below a kept leaf is dropped and an object with no legible scalar fields keeps the previous marker.
gates.failureFallback: Objects with nothing legible to keep fall back to the original "[object]" marker, and thumbnail/base64 fields remain stripped.

gates.protects: A transient provider failure that the engine is retrying is narrated to the user (model service, reason, attempt count) instead of appearing as unexplained silence.
gates.baseline: Only the transient family is narrated as a retry; genuine configuration errors still reach the normal terminal-failure classification unchanged, and the full stderr line still lands in the log.
gates.failureFallback: An unparseable or chunk-split line, a non-ERROR level, or a missing/foreign session id yields no notice at all — log-only, exactly as before.

gates.protects: A plain question reaches the model without payload-free prompt layers padding it or a false scheduled-task classification inserting an extra blocking model call first.
gates.baseline: Every layer that has real payload still ships unchanged, the user_original_request anchor always exists, and genuine scheduled-task phrasing is still recognized.
gates.failureFallback: A missed scheduled-task classification routes the message down the ordinary agent path; layer suppression only ever removes blocks whose body is empty.

gates.protects: An image question is bridged concurrently rather than one model call per image, and the answering model is told it never saw the images so it cannot invent detail the description omits.
gates.baseline: Recognition order is identical to the serial bridge, payload and evidence accounting are unchanged, and native-vision models still receive the real image untouched.
gates.failureFallback: A blank recognition counts as failed, an invalid concurrency value clamps to one lane, and any bridge failure keeps the original image for a native-vision retry.

gates.protects: A user pinned to a text-only model learns why an image question is slow and which model they own would read the image directly, instead of silently paying for the vision bridge.
gates.baseline: Auto selection still routes image turns to a vision-capable model on its own, and a manual model pick is never overridden.
gates.failureFallback: No catalog, no alternative, already on the only vision model, or any lookup error drops the advice clause; the bridge behaves exactly as before.

gates.protects: Typing hints, read receipts and reactions work end to end, and the record of WHICH layer was actually missing survives so the transport is not re-implemented.
gates.baseline: All three are additive: durable sync, unread counts, edit/revoke conflict detection and reply snapshots behave exactly as before, and an older client skips the new reaction event while still advancing its cursor.
gates.failureFallback: A missed typing frame degrades to nobody typing; unknown membership or absent reports yield no double tick; a reaction that fails to commit is corrected by the next sync; every reader fails open rather than throwing.

gates.protects: The collaboration panel stays readable and clickable: metadata never shrinks below 11px, interactive chips never below 24px, and every colour comes from a theme token so contrast follows the theme.
gates.baseline: Purely presentational. No message, sync, unread or reaction behaviour depends on these values; a violation is a legibility regression, never a loss of function.
gates.failureFallback: The check reads declared values from the stylesheet, so it holds for panel states no fixture renders. A deliberate exception is allowed only by naming the selector and its reason in the test's exemption map, which itself fails once the selector disappears.

gates.protects: A message attachment shows its name, size and type — and a thumbnail once its bytes are local — instead of N identical Download buttons. The record of WHERE that metadata lives survives: the server already had original_name/mime_type from object init, so only the history projection was missing; it is NOT an end-to-end payload problem, because history is the server's authorized plaintext view and a sender-side encrypted payload would never reach the recipient.
gates.baseline: Strictly additive. `attachmentIds` is unchanged in content and order, so addressing, authorization, download, revocation and reply snapshots behave exactly as before; an older server sends no metadata and every card falls back to the plain download action that shipped previously.
gates.failureFallback: Metadata is descriptive and never an input to access: it is re-derived at the IPC boundary against the ids actually projected, withheld entirely for a revoked message on BOTH sides, dropped (never sanitized) when a name carries path parts, bounded at 20 rows, and the server join is a LEFT join so a missing object row cannot shorten the id list. A thumbnail is only attempted for an image type and only from a finished download; an unresolved preview leaves the drawn glyph and the download action.

gates.protects: Contacts and Teams read as an address book: 56px rows, A–Z pinyin sections, pending requests behind one counted entry, destructive actions off the row, one search box, and no internal scope id ever printed to a person.
gates.baseline: Presentation and information architecture only. Every command still goes through the same friend/conversation APIs with the same confirmations and permission checks; the pinyin sectioning is derived from the display name and touches no identity or authorization value.
gates.failureFallback: Sectioning degrades, never breaks: a build without ICU's pinyin collation falls back to a locale collator so Latin names still section and Han names land in one bucket together, and malformed input yields an empty list rather than a throw (this runs on every keystroke). A contact with no name still gets a row. Actions are visible without hover where there is no pointer.

gates.protects: The three destinations are a persistent icon rail instead of a hamburger popover, and a group's avatar is composed from its members instead of the first character of its title.
gates.baseline: Presentation only. The rail reuses the same three tab buttons, ids and aria-controls that the popover held, so section switching, navigation generations and every load path are unchanged; the roster is a new read on an existing local table and no server call or permission decision depends on it.
gates.failureFallback: The roster is a drawing input and fails open at every step: a failed read yields no rosters rather than throwing inside the conversation list, malformed rows are skipped, the list is capped at 9 per conversation, ids are re-validated and re-bounded at the IPC boundary, and fewer than two resolved names falls back to exactly the single-initial tile that shipped before — never an empty square. A direct chat is excluded by kind.

gates.protects: Every people-picker in the collaboration panel is a real picker — group creation, team channel creation and adding a member — with search, avatars, A–Z sections and a visible selection; a group refuses to be created with nobody in it, and its name is optional.
gates.baseline: The command is unchanged — same conversation.create action, scope, kind and permission checks. Only the control that gathers members and the title default changed, and both were already permitted by the server (empty title accepted, no minimum member count).
gates.failureFallback: The picker holds selection outside the DOM, so filtering or a roster refresh cannot silently drop a chosen person; a contact who becomes unselectable is removed from the selection rather than submitted invisibly. A blank name derives from the member names WITHOUT going through i18n, because `t()` returns its key when no locale has loaded and the key would become the group's name; the derived title is cut to the server's 200-character cap. The empty-selection rule is enforced in the submit handler as well as on the button, since a disabled button is bypassed by requestSubmit(). A channel has no minimum (it may start with only its creator) and a PUBLIC channel hides the picker entirely, because its membership is the whole team. Adding a member is single-select, since the command takes one target per call and a partly applied batch has no story in this UI. Unfinished channel forms survive a background sync: the picked members are snapshotted and restored separately from the text fields, and no picker input carries a `name`, so a name-matched draft restore can never target one.

gates.protects: Adding a contact shows you WHO you are about to add before anything is sent, lets you send a greeting with the request, and lets you copy your own Lily ID — the only handle by which anyone can add you.
gates.baseline: Additive. The request command is unchanged apart from an optional greeting the server already accepted; the lookup is a new READ that persists nothing, so no outbox row, receipt or retry path is involved. A build whose server lacks the lookup route degrades to the previous behaviour: the form reports the id as unavailable rather than breaking.
gates.failureFallback: The lookup fails closed at every step: a malformed id is refused locally so it never spends a server rate-limit slot, an empty or partial profile is 'unavailable' rather than a half-rendered person, a transport refusal (including the rate limit) reaches the caller intact, a switched account aborts instead of answering with the previous account's result, and a superseded lookup cannot paint over a newer one. Editing the id invalidates the confirmation, so a request can never be addressed to someone other than the person shown.

gates.protects: A conversation never scrolls sideways, and the hover action overlay stays inside the thread in both directions no matter how many actions a message offers.
gates.baseline: Geometry only. Every action still exists and is still reachable; the overlay wraps instead of extending past the thread.
gates.failureFallback: The overlay is absolutely positioned, so it shrink-to-fits inside its row: once its content may wrap it cannot exceed that box, whatever the action count or panel width. Anchoring is to the side of the row that has room — incoming rows grow right, outgoing rows grow left — so neither edge is crossed. A long unbroken URL wraps rather than widening the thread.

gates.protects: One screen shows one thing: exactly one title names where you are, and a roster or a pending-request list is its own screen with a back button rather than content appended into the list it came from. A hidden view occupies nothing, and the reader is never shown an invented identity.
gates.baseline: Structure only. Every destination, roster and request is still reachable by the same actions and the same commands; only where they draw changed.
gates.failureFallback: The detail surface is optional: each view falls back to the inline container it always used when no detail view is supplied, which is how these modules render standalone in the DOM tests. Changing destination closes any open detail, so a roster from one list can never be left over on another. Each panel view sets its own `display`, which outranks the hidden attribute's UA rule, so every one of them opts back in explicitly — and that is checked by MEASURING the rendered box, shown and hidden, rather than by grepping for the rule. With no profile loaded there is no identity row at all: `identityName`'s fallback names an unknown user, which is a fair placeholder for someone else and nonsense for yourself.

gates.protects: The collaboration stylesheet has no declarations that can never take effect, and the number of selectors styled in more than one block cannot quietly grow.
gates.baseline: Verified as a no-op by a rendered fingerprint — the computed style of every element in the panel across eight states and both themes — which is byte-identical before and after. Nothing about the rendering changed.
gates.failureFallback: The check is deliberately narrow so it cannot be wrong: dead means the SAME selector text declares the SAME property again later at TOP LEVEL, with neither marked !important. Identical selector text means an identical match set, so the later declaration always wins. Rules inside @media are excluded on both sides, since one of those does not unconditionally override anything. Shorthands are compared as written, not expanded.

gates.protects: The panel can be dragged wide enough for the desktop-chat shape — rail, list and thread all on screen — and then keeps the list beside the thread instead of replacing it. Below the threshold it stays one column, which is the only thing that fits at 420px.
gates.baseline: The narrow behaviour is unchanged: one column, a conversation replaces the list, and the back button returns to it. Nothing about messaging, loading or permissions is involved — only how many columns the panel lays out.
gates.failureFallback: Two panes are docked-only, since an overlay panel covers the workbench and splitting it there would leave both halves narrow. The width ceiling always reserves space for the workbench beside the panel, so the panel cannot eat the window; the reserve is verified in a window narrow enough for it to bind rather than one where the absolute cap is the smaller of the two. Crossing the threshold in either direction re-lays out an already-open conversation, and the back button comes back with the one-column layout.

gates.protects: The collaboration panel can be opened in a window of its own, presenting only the panel, without a second copy of its markup and without building the workbench behind it.
gates.baseline: Purely additive. The docked panel is unchanged; the detached window reuses the same renderer entry, the same modules and the same IPC. No service change was needed: `collaboration:subscribe` already keyed its subscriptions by `sender` and handed each one its own unsubscribe, so a second window subscribes independently.
gates.failureFallback: One window at a time — opening again focuses the existing one rather than making a second view of the same list. A remembered position is only reused when part of the window would still be reachable on a display that exists; that predicate is exported and tested directly, because macOS clamps an off-screen window by itself and a test that reads bounds back could not tell whether the check ran. Bounds failing to persist costs a remembered position, never an error. The detached window skips the workbench boot rather than hiding it, so a second window does not duplicate its pollers, model lists and session UI.

gates.protects: The workbench keeps one type scale and one radius scale. Sizes that ARE scale values (11/12/13/15px, 4/6/10/14/999px) must be written as the token, so the text-size setting reaches them and a scale change is one edit; off-scale literals, sub-11px text, odd font weights, literal shadows and magic z-index are counted per stylesheet and may only decrease.
gates.baseline: Purely presentational. No behaviour reads these values; a violation is a consistency regression, never a loss of function. At default text size a token and its literal render identically (verified by computed-style fingerprint across every settings page, 950 elements, 2026-09-03).
gates.failureFallback: Static: reads declared values from every stylesheet, so it holds for screens no fixture renders. The ratchet baseline can only be lowered by regenerating it on purpose (--write-baseline); a count that rises fails with the file and property named.

gates.protects: The every-turn agent guide keeps room for its skill index. The index is what tells the model which skills exist; it is built last from whatever bytes the fixed prefix leaves over, so a growing prefix silently deletes skills from what the model can see. At supported scale (bundled skills, and bundled plus the whole installable catalog, in zh-CN/en/ar) no skill may be dropped or left undescribed, the guide stays under 95% of AGENT_GUIDE_MAX_BYTES, and per-configuration bytes may only fall.
gates.baseline: Measured, not assumed: today the worst realistic configuration is Arabic with the full catalog at 41976B, 85.4% of the 49152B budget, 42 of 42 skills indexed, and room for only about 13 more average skills — the per-skill cost is taken from the real index lines, since a synthetic probe skill has no SKILL.md on disk and omits the guide path every real entry carries, which read half the true cost. The pre-existing assertion only checked bytes <= AGENT_GUIDE_MAX_BYTES, which the builder guarantees by amputating the index, so it could never fail however many skills were being discarded.
gates.failureFallback: Static and deterministic: builds the real guide from the real skill directories, no model and no network. Reads the omission report the builder now fills, so a dropped skill is named rather than counted. The byte ratchet can only be raised by regenerating the baseline on purpose (--write-baseline). Mutation-verified 2026-09-04: a 4KB prefix growth, a budget cut to 30KB, and one description-less skill each fail the gate with the cause named. A companion guard, test-skill-capacity-notice.mjs, covers the user-facing half: the runtime measurement writes nothing, reports null rather than Infinity when no skill is indexed, and reaches the skills page through skills:list, where a measurement failure returns null instead of breaking the list. Mutation-verified: raising the notice threshold, dropping the danger tone, and removing the fail-open catch each fail.

gates.protects: The mandatory guide bodies ride every prompt, and rules are pushed rather than pulled — a rule the model was never shown is a rule it violates. A manifest may split its guide into addressable blocks with an `appliesTo` condition so a block that provably cannot apply here stops shipping, but pruning may never happen on a guess: an unknown condition key, a section that would prune to nothing, or a manifest with no blocks all keep the full body.
gates.baseline: Value-preserving where it prunes. Windows PowerShell rules were hardcoded inside one monolithic body string and shipped in every prompt on macOS and Linux, where they cannot apply. Verified 2026-09-04 across zh-CN/en/ar: a win32 install gets a byte-for-byte identical guide, and a darwin install differs by exactly the Windows section (480B zh, 455B en, 0B ar, which never had one). Arabic keeps `body` with no blocks, proving the unconverted path is unchanged.
gates.failureFallback: Static and deterministic, no model and no network. `body` stays in the manifest as the authoritative text AND the fallback for every uncertain path, and the gate asserts blocks rejoin to it byte-for-byte, so blocks cannot drift into shipping different rules. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04: making an unknown condition prune, removing the prune-to-nothing fallback, inverting the platform match, drifting a block from its body, and letting the Windows block swallow the trailing skill-directory paragraph each fail with the cause named.

gates.protects: The ruler for whether a guide change made the model dumber. Rules are pushed, not pulled, so the precondition for the model obeying a rule is that the rule is still in the assembled guide: agent-guide-rule-contract.json anchors ten non-negotiable rules on distinctive shipped phrases and the guide is rebuilt across three locales and three platforms to prove each required rule is present and each environment-conditional one is absent where it cannot apply. A separate live suite measures whether the model then obeys, and this gate keeps that suite honest offline.
gates.baseline: Deterministic and credential-free, so it runs on every change rather than only on release. Measured 2026-09-04: nine of ten rules present in all 9 locale x platform builds; windows-shell present in 2 of 9 (win32 zh-CN and en) exactly as agent-guide-blocks intends. It also surfaced a real gap now recorded in the contract rather than tolerated silently: the Arabic guide never contained a Windows section, so an Arabic user on Windows receives no PowerShell shell rules.
gates.failureFallback: Static: reads the real skill directories and rebuilds the real guide, no model and no network. Guards itself against becoming vacuous — an anchor matching in NO configuration fails as a dead contract entry, an unanchored locale fails as an unmeasured locale, every live-eval grader must score its own pass/fail fixtures and reject empty output, every discovery prompt must share no wording with its target skill's description, and every rule case must point at a tracked rule. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04: deleting a rule from the guide, making the Windows block unconditional, pointing an anchor at absent text, dropping a locale anchor, a grader that always passes, a discovery prompt that echoes its target description, an untracked rule reference, and removing the canary each fail by name.

gates.protects: The permission mode the user chose must reach the model. permissionMode drove tool auto-approval and runtime identity only and never appeared in the prompt, so a session the user explicitly set to 全自主 still ended turns by handing the decision back. Only "full" adds a directive; "ask" and "plan" describe sessions where the user wants to be consulted and get nothing added, so they are byte-identical to before, and an unknown mode gets nothing rather than inheriting autonomy instructions.
gates.baseline: Reported from the field 2026-09-04: a 全自主 session closed with "要我接着做前端（#9）还是先跑一遍全量 mvn test?" while the model's own task list still showed 8/10 done. Live A/B on deepseek-v4-pro, 5 runs per arm with a deliberately neutral prompt: without the directive the turn decided and carried on 2 of 5 times, with it 5 of 5. An earlier version of the case scored 3/5 vs 4/5 because its prompt itself said "那个细节你定成哪一种" and therefore instructed the decision it was meant to measure.
gates.failureFallback: Additive and fail-open: the wiring is wrapped so any failure leaves the per-prompt guidance exactly as before rather than breaking the turn, and non-full modes receive nothing. test-agent-autonomy-guidance.mjs asserts only "full" produces a block, that stray whitespace does not silently downgrade the user's choice, that unlisted locales fall back to English and never to Chinese, and that the wiring passes the session's real mode and stays inside a catch. The rule is registered in agent-guide-rule-contract.json with source "autonomy-guidance", so test-agent-guide-rule-contract.mjs checks it against its real carrier across all three modes: required in full, absent in ask and plan.

gates.protects: A leaked tool call must not kill a turn that already did work. The rescue for MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT replays the user's request, which is only safe when every tool that ran was replay-safe, so a long turn that had already edited files got no rescue at all. Continuing the same engine session re-does nothing — history and files remain — and asks only for the missing next action.
gates.baseline: Reported from the field 2026-09-04: 148 tool calls into a turn, files already edited, the model wrote its next tool call as plain text and the turn died with no output. Replay would have re-run the edits, so the side-effect guard refusing was correct; failing was not the only alternative. Strictly additive — such turns previously received no rescue whatsoever, so the worst case is the behaviour they already had.
gates.failureFallback: Continuation is narrow by construction: only MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT, only when the run was NOT side-effect free (read-only turns keep the cleaner replay), and never for the other healable codes. Kill switch LILY_TOOL_CALL_CONTINUATION=0 restores the previous failure. The side-effect guard still refuses every REPLAY. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04: continuing read-only turns, dropping the do-not-redo instruction, moving the decision after the guard so it becomes unreachable, sending the user's original message as the continuation content, and a broken kill switch each fail by name.

gates.protects: Deleting a conversation must delete its runtime events, and the orphan backlog must drain. Runtime events were INSERTed and UPDATEd but never DELETEd anywhere in the repo, and clearing a session removed only its messages — so every deleted conversation left its whole event stream behind permanently, on the main-process database every turn writes to. Growth is now stopped at the source: when a turn reaches a terminal state its live-painting events (assistant.delta, assistant.thinking.delta, task.step.progress, process.event, subagent.event) are deleted in the same write. That list is an ALLOWLIST, never an exclusion list, because getProjectedConversation LEFT JOINs runtime_events for the six turn.* terminal types and rebuilds a past turn's assistant text from that payload. A pre-retention install's existing backlog drains silently in the background, bounded by the PRIMARY KEY so each chunk is an index range scan, with a cursor in schema_meta that resumes across restarts and stops looking once finished.
gates.baseline: Measured on a real install 2026-09-04: messages.db was 12 GB holding 1,156 messages and 3,917,891 runtime events across 155 sessions, while only 29 sessions still had messages — 2,542,720 events (64.9%) orphaned from 135 deleted conversations. The top types are per-token streaming telemetry with no consumer once a turn ends: process.event 1,457,033, task.step.progress 1,158,734, assistant.thinking.delta 936,587. The pre-existing maintenance only compacted oversized payloads; it never removed a row. The first implementation of the backlog drain caused a regression that proves why this is gated: it deleted row by row, and node:sqlite is synchronous on the main process, so 20,000 statements per round x 50 rounds removed exactly 1,000,000 rows and froze the UI for the first two minutes after a restart. Deleting whole sessions instead costs ~0 ms (4 statements for 954 rows, indexed by session_id), but DISCOVERING orphans costs a full scan of the event table — 3,133 ms with GROUP BY, 2,821 ms via DISTINCT — which cannot be made cheap on the main process. So the backlog drain is opt-in (LILY_PRUNE_ORPHAN_EVENTS=1) while clear() prevents new orphans at zero cost. Composition measured the same day: of 2,996,807 events, 51.5% were orphans and 48.5% belonged to live sessions — but 98.2% of those live ones were pure streaming deltas and 1,375,646 belonged to turns already finished. Payload volume 7.34 GB, of which 99.5% is reclaimable. The only consumer of runtime_events is the control server's waitForEvents long-poll, which tails a turn while it RUNS; history rendering reads turn_projection and messages instead. The obvious backlog query is a trap: DELETE ... WHERE type IN (...) is a full table SCAN because nothing indexes `type` — 19,835 ms measured for the equivalent scan over 2,923,716 matching rows on the real 12 GB file, on a synchronous main-process connection. Bounding by session_id + a seq range turns it into SEARCH ... USING INDEX: 30 ms for a 20,000-seq window matching 19,726 rows, so the whole 2.9 M rows is ~150 windows, about 4.5 s of work delivered 30 ms at a time. This also corrects an earlier claim of mine: compaction alone would NOT have shrunk that install, because the freelist held only 2.11 GB (17.4%) — below the 25% threshold, so it would not even have run, and at best 12.14 GB would have become 10.03 GB. Deleting the 7.16 GB of ephemeral payload first is what makes the file reach ~2.9 GB.
gates.failureFallback: Safe by construction: the only reader, getRuntimeEvents, is always scoped to a session id, so events belonging to a session that no longer exists cannot affect anything live, and the prune deletes only rows with no surviving message. Bounded per call (default 20,000, hard-capped) so a large backlog is worked off across rounds and startups instead of blocking one, and wrapped so a failure logs and leaves startup alone. Retention and the maintenance loop were extracted to src/main/store/runtime-event-retention.js and runtime-event-maintenance.js because message-store.js and session-manager.js were at their line ratchets; the loop takes its store and scheduler by injection, so the gate drives it directly and asserts orphans are pruned BEFORE payloads are compacted and that the first round is deferred. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04, seven ways: clear no longer dropping events, an unbounded prune, a prune that ignores whether messages survive, a clear that wipes other sessions' events, removing the scheduling so the method is never called, reversing the job order, and a first round with no delay each fail by name. Per-turn pruning is scoped by BOTH session_id and turn_id (verified against a concurrently running turn in the same session and another session using the same turn id — an earlier fixture had neither, so dropping either predicate passed), and LILY_PRUNE_TURN_EVENTS=0 restores the previous behaviour. The historical drain is asserted on its QUERY SHAPE, not only its behaviour — a type-only DELETE removes the same rows and passes any behavioural test, so the gate matches the session_id + seq predicate in source AND checks EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reports USING INDEX rather than SCAN. It supersedes the orphan scan, which stays opt-in only as an escape hatch. Kill switch LILY_PRUNE_EVENT_HISTORY=0.

gates.protects: Engine serves left by an ungraceful exit are reaped at startup, and a LIVE serve is never touched. before-quit already reaps the shared serve, but it only runs on a graceful quit — Ctrl-C on the dev launcher, a crash, or a force quit skips it and the serve survives reparented to init, holding userData files and a port. Nothing ever looked for what a previous run left behind.
gates.baseline: Measured on a real dev machine 2026-09-04: 7 orphaned serves, the oldest 40 days old, dragging 24 stale Electron children, 587 MB resident, with 19 processes holding files under userData at once — the same class of problem as the Windows updater's "could not be closed". After a manual sweep, 40 processes became 9 and orphans went to 0; the live app was unaffected and every stale process exited on SIGTERM without needing SIGKILL.
gates.failureFallback: The value is in what it REFUSES. All three conditions must hold: the command starts with exactly this install's bundled binary AND ends at a word boundary, the parent is gone (ppid 1), and the pid is neither ours nor our parent's. A live instance's serve is parented to that instance, so it can never match — and the call sits after the single-instance lock, which is what proves a parentless serve is an orphan rather than a concurrently starting instance. An absent or relative binary path selects nothing rather than guessing. win32 is a deliberate no-op because a dead parent's pid is not rewritten to 1 there, so the safety condition cannot be evaluated. Fail-open: any error returns 0 and logs, and one un-killable pid does not stop the rest. Kill switch LILY_REAP_ORPHAN_SERVES=0. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04, six ways: dropping the ppid check, a bare startsWith (which reaped ".../opencode-old serve"), dropping the serve check, accepting a relative path, removing the win32 no-op, and a broken kill switch each fail by name. Two of those found real defects in the implementation and in the gate's own fixture.

gates.protects: Disk is reclaimed from messages.db without an exclusive lock, and never at the cost of a row. Deleting rows returns pages to SQLite's freelist but never shrinks the FILE, so an install that once bloated stays bloated. VACUUM rebuilds in place under an exclusive lock, which is unacceptable for a customer with a 12 GB file; VACUUM INTO reads the source and writes a compacted copy, so nothing is write-locked and the disk required is the size of the RESULT. The swap runs before the store's first open, the only moment a rename cannot race a reader.
gates.baseline: Measured on a real install 2026-09-04: 12.14 GB holding 1,156 messages, 7.34 GB of it runtime_events payloads, 99.5% reclaimable. Verified end to end on a 247 MB fixture bloated the same way (write many rows, delete them): the file stayed 247 MB after the deletes, and compaction brought it to 0.5 MB with every remaining row and messages intact and no leftover files.
gates.failureFallback: A compaction that cannot prove itself does nothing. Five gates before the swap: the file must be large enough to be worth copying, the freelist must actually hold reclaimable pages, the copy must pass PRAGMA integrity_check, row counts for messages/turn_inputs/turn_projection/runtime_events/blobs/message_blobs must MATCH the source, and only then a rename — with the original kept under .precompact until the rename lands and restored if it fails. Any refusal deletes its copy so a failed attempt cannot eat the disk it was trying to free. Fail-open: an internal error returns a reason instead of throwing into startup, and the store opens regardless. Kill switch LILY_COMPACT_MESSAGE_DB=0. Mutation-verified 2026-09-04, six ways: skipping the row-count comparison, skipping integrity_check, dropping the freelist threshold, leaving the copy behind on refusal, moving the call after the store opens, and a broken kill switch each fail by name.

gates.protects: An enterprise can hand a seat to staff who have no account yet, and a seat is never granted or lost by accident. POST members accepted {userId | phoneE164} but organization_members references users(id), so an unregistered phone was a dead end (USER_NOT_FOUND 404) and a company that bought seats had to wait for every employee to sign up and add them one at a time. An invitation records the intent; the seat is granted at that person's next successful login.
gates.baseline: Purely additive. One new table (migration 043); organization_members is untouched, so every existing membership path behaves exactly as before and an install that never creates an invitation is unchanged. A registered phone still becomes a membership immediately rather than being made to wait for a login it does not need. The design doc never covered this case — no mention of invite/provisioning anywhere in its 284 lines — so this is a design gap being closed, not an implementation drift.
gates.failureFallback: Login never depends on it: redemption runs AFTER the login transaction commits, inside its own try, so a seat that cannot be granted leaves the invitation pending for the next login instead of failing the login. Each invitation redeems in its own transaction with a FOR UPDATE re-read, so two devices logging in at once cannot both grant the same seat, and the membership insert is onConflict-doNothing idempotent. A disabled organization DEFERS rather than consuming — the seat was paid for and the org may be re-enabled. Ownership is refused explicitly (INVITE_ROLE_UNSUPPORTED) rather than silently normalised down to member, and the table's own CHECK forbids it. Uniqueness is a PARTIAL index on pending only, so accepted/revoked rows stay for audit without blocking a re-invite, and invited_by is ON DELETE SET NULL so an invitation outlives the admin who sent it. Mutation-verified 2026-09-05, six ways: routing a registered phone through an invitation, consuming instead of deferring on a disabled org, dropping the row lock, allowing an owner invitation, moving redemption inside the login transaction, and making the unique index non-partial each fail by name.

gates.protects: A company can generate dedicated accounts for staff — login name plus a one-time password — and those accounts are never a weaker door than a phone. Identity was phone-only (users.phone_e164 NOT NULL UNIQUE, SMS-only login), so 'the company creates the account' was impossible. Issued accounts are owned by the organization: removing or disabling the membership locks the login, while a phone user who merely joined keeps their own account. Batches may be named by prefix and numbered sequentially (MAX + 20 -> max_0001..max_0020), continuing after the last batch.
gates.baseline: Additive: phone_e164 becomes nullable but every existing row has one, a CHECK keeps every user reachable by some identity, and the login-name unique index is partial so phone-only users are untouched. Password login mirrors the SMS route's device handling and session shape so the client treats both identically. The 5-strike lock matches the SMS path, and the lock rejects even a CORRECT password until it expires. An unknown login name returns the same code as a wrong password, and the decision is computed before the existence check, so names cannot be probed by response or timing.
gates.failureFallback: scrypt with a per-user random salt (Node built-in, no dependency); a malformed stored hash verifies false rather than throwing on the login path; initial passwords use an alphabet with no 0/O/1/l/I and are returned once — the gate counts BOTH write sites (provision and reset) go through hashPassword, because a regex matching either site let plaintext at one slip through. Changing a password requires the current one, so a stolen session alone cannot take over the account. Owner can never be issued. service-client.js was at its ratchet, so the six account-auth calls were extracted to service-client-account-auth.js with transport and device identity injected. Mutation-verified 2026-09-05, seven ways: honouring a correct password while locked, a fixed salt, not locking an issued account on removal, a distinct unknown-user error code, skipping the current-password check on change, storing the initial password as-is at the reset site, and allowing an owner to be issued — each fails by name. Sequential numbering is resolved server-side under the organization lock so two admins cannot both take 0001, continues from the highest number already issued under that prefix in THIS organization (scoped by provisioned_organization_id), skips hand-taken numbers, is at least 4 digits and widens past 9999, and is capped at the batch limit. Five further mutations fail by name: restarting at 0001, dropping the org scope, fixing the width, removing the cap, and issuing owners in a batch.

gates.protects: The platform admin can create an organization for a customer and hand it to its first owner, without the §7.1 boundary eroding. Before, creation was self-serve only — an operator who had signed a customer could not open the enterprise; someone at the customer had to register, create, and become owner themselves. The owner is named exactly one of two ways: a registered phone, or an account the platform issues on the spot.
gates.baseline: Additive: one admin POST, one web form, one shared reveal component. The admin surface still has NO member endpoints — after the handoff, members are the owner's business alone, which is the part of §7.1 that mattered. Owner issuance is a narrow opening (allowOwner) that only this route passes; the enterprise-side provisioning path never does, so a company admin cannot mint owners. An unregistered owner phone is refused with OWNER_NOT_REGISTERED rather than turned into an invitation (which cannot carry owner) or a silently invented seat.
gates.failureFallback: test-admin-enterprise-create.mjs asserts the opening is off by default and passed only by the admin route, that the route is behind assertAdmin, audited (including whether the owner was issued), never persists the initial password, and that no member endpoint exists on the admin surface. The closed loop is admin-enterprise-create-integration.mjs against a real Postgres with the real migrations: admin creates -> issued owner logs in with the one-time password -> is forced to change it -> the organization appears in the owner's list and the admin's list. The integration ran green first time against PostgreSQL 16 with all 44 migrations (11 steps); it skips cleanly where DATABASE_URL is absent, so listing it here never fails a DB-less run.

gates.protects: Skill declarations reach preparation only for explicit task selections without turning every enabled or recommended skill into heavy downloads.
gates.baseline: The hardcoded skill map and existing task readiness remain the baseline.
gates.failureFallback: Fresh bounded own-ID validation; malformed schema/identity and per-source failures preserve registry/legacy sources. LILY_SKILL_RUNTIME_DECLARATIONS=0 restores pre-change readiness including selected legacy skills. Verified mutations: remove known-ID validation, legacy union, selection forwarding and kill switch.

gates.protects: Workspace guides stay inside the workspace, obey explicit conversation selection and never displace platform context.
gates.baseline: Workspace skill directories were not discovered; platform guide and learned sections must remain intact.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_WORKSPACE_SKILLS=0 or discovery errors leave existing guidance unchanged. Content hashes and selected local IDs invalidate session cache; final budget reserves learned sections. Mutations removing realpath checks, content hashing, local selection signature, kill switch and both reservation safeguards fail named behavioral assertions.

gates.protects: Same-workspace conversations cannot regain a disabled skill through a shared native registry or stale local guide.
gates.baseline: Native skill paths stay empty; explicit conversation skills are authoritative.
gates.failureFallback: The engine native registry remains unmounted. Real session guide tests cover two conversations, local enable/disable, content edits and removal; mutation dropping local IDs from cache signature fails. No brittle engine session-keyword absence test.

gates.protects: Long descriptions retain bounded routing exclusions without removing any previously discoverable skill.
gates.baseline: The original 180-character description index is preserved if expansion cannot fit.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_GUIDE_INDEX_NEGATIVE=0 restores exact old output. Enhancement exceptions or budget eviction revert to original index; all three languages retain existing headroom. Mutation allowing eviction fails. First-party descriptions are independently checked for short task-oriented content.

gates.protects: Real missing dependencies get actionable managed recovery without misclassifying input files, missing cwd, printed examples or inherited catalog keys.
gates.baseline: Failed bash output is preserved and the model can continue using existing tools.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_RUNTIME_DEP_HINT=0, unknown shapes or detection failures preserve output. Integer nonzero engine exit plus precise diagnostics are required; session dedup is bounded and clears on deletion or successful retry. Mutations remove dedup, own-property checks, exit evidence or Windows/Node detection, reintroduce ambiguous ENOENT or corrupt maps; each fails.

gates.protects: A started background pack job is not reported ready; terminal failures remain observable and retries use freshly resolved managed environment.
gates.baseline: Existing background installer and artifact integrity/health checks remain authoritative.
gates.failureFallback: Broad lists never health-probe every pack. Targeted verification exposes safe environment keys only after successful health; bundled read-only repair refuses before starting. Real Python missing import then managed-environment retry and deferred installer failure are exercised. Mutations reporting starting as ready, dropping terminal state or bundled repair guard fail.

gates.protects: Advisory candidate matching cannot masquerade as model selection, successful reads or completed tasks.
gates.baseline: Legacy audits contain path attempts but no reliable outcome; those observations stay unknown.
gates.failureFallback: Pure aggregation never controls execution. SQLite reports are read-only and support real gzip envelopes; invalid rows counted, unknowns excluded from rate. Mutations treating failed reads as success or unknowns as known denominator fail. Actual tool.done provenance survives archive mapping; real router/finalizer/archive tests prevent terminal cleanup or missing status from fabricating success or failure. Removing the provenance mapping fails an isolated in-memory mutation.

gates.protects: Discovery evals require actual successful guide-read tool events rather than text merely naming a skill.
gates.baseline: Answer-only discovery cannot prove the guide was used.
gates.failureFallback: Structured CLI event collection fails loud on unavailable events, errors or mixed sessions; missing/wrong/failed guide reads fail discovery checks. Live credentials remain separate from deterministic fixture gates. Mutation skipping read-evidence check fails.

gates.protects: Enterprise membership and online indicators use current authorization and real expiring connections.
gates.baseline: Existing personal contacts and messaging remain available when the directory endpoint is unavailable.
gates.failureFallback: Offline caches show unknown presence; removed membership is not resurrected by network failures; nickname updates preserve existing Lily IDs.

gates.protects: Authorized, expiring IM presence across server instances with exact session/device binding and bounded Redis queries.
gates.baseline: PostgreSQL remains authoritative for messages, outbox and access control; presence is advisory and does not persist message content.
gates.failureFallback: Redis failure or uncertain leases return unknown instead of false offline; durable messaging continues and old connections cannot erase replacement leases.

gates.protects: IM lists and headers name people and conversations the way a colleague recognises them. A 1:1 has no stored title and used to show the raw conversation id — a long opaque string — in the inbox, the Teams channel list, the forward picker and the thread header; a person without a nickname was shown by Lily handle or an opaque placeholder. Now a conversation is named after its other member(s) and a person by nickname → enterprise login → server-masked phone (138****5678) → handle, never a raw id. The Teams view no longer rebuilds on sync events that changed nothing visible (typing ticks, read receipts, the 15 s directory poll, onlineUntil advancing), and a real rebuild keeps open channel forms.
gates.baseline: Reported 2026-09-05: '会话会展示一大长串' (inbox rows showed conv_… ids for every direct chat) and '在 team 里跳来跳去' (teams.update() did list.replaceChildren() on every load(); socialDirty was set on every state event and a 15 s poll). Server rows carried no login/phone facets at all, so nothing better than lilyId was available to show. Strictly additive: rows without the new facets normalise to empty strings and every previous fallback still applies; the fingerprint short-circuit can only skip a rebuild whose inputs are byte-identical, and revocation handling runs before it on every update. The live enterprise directory carries the same facets (probe-gated on migration 044) and the desktop merge keeps local facets when a live row lacks them.
gates.failureFallback: Phone is masked server-side (identity-fields.js) before any row leaves; the raw number is never sent or cached, and the existing leak guards were tightened to reject phoneE164/phone_e164 while allowing the masked facet. The users join is probe-gated so a database without migration 044 keeps bootstrapping (the real-Postgres sync integration, which builds a minimal users table, caught the unconditional version). Mention-candidate items keep their old exact key set because shipped clients validate them strictly; the client allowlist was extended for forward compatibility. A service stop during the in-flight live directory read yields the stopped result instead of a rejection. Mutation-verified 2026-09-05: dropping the identical-payload short-circuit, admitting onlineUntil into the fingerprint, forgetting the enterprise login in the chain, falling back to the conversation id, keeping placeholders in group titles, searching the stored title instead of the displayed one, forgetting open forms across a rebuild, and removing the scroll restore each fail by name (the scroll test forces layout while empty — a synchronous refill never loses the offset, which is exactly the vacuous assertion the first version had).

gates.protects: Confirmed repetitive text and unchanged job inspection cannot keep a task alive indefinitely; terminal job receipts retire historical running blockers.
gates.baseline: Evolving work, foreground tool leases, pending user input, structured/quoted/requested content and unknown observations retain existing behavior. No model downgrade or tool replay.
gates.failureFallback: Bounded per-turn observation fails open on malformed/oversized data; kill switch restores baseline. Confirmed stops retain partial output and reason, use the existing bounded abort, never stop background jobs or automatically re-enter parent recovery.

gates.protects: The task-list progress card cannot be confidently wrong when the model forgets to update its list. Field case 2026-09-05: one todowrite, eight more tool calls, card stuck at 0/7 while four steps were done. The platform now (1) nudges the model inside the tool result after N calls without a todowrite, naming the steps the execution record already supports (todo-progress-nudge plugin); (2) overlays execution evidence on the plan — a step is 'evidenced' only when a SUCCESSFUL tool call's input contains every identifier unique to that step; (3) reconciles at turn end: stale 'in progress' becomes 'unconfirmed', and a bounded model pass may settle undecided steps only with a quote literally present in the evidence; (4) states staleness in the summary. All four are display/nudge overlays: the model's own list is never rewritten.
gates.baseline: Without a taskRun or with the default scaffold plan the strip and card render exactly as before (same summary, same icons, same classes). Steps without a unique identifier are never inferred; shared identifiers prove nothing; a failed final attempt proves nothing; output-only mentions are not evidence. A fresh todowrite drops every overlay — the model's statuses win.
gates.failureFallback: Plugin and library fail open (try/catch on every hook call, bounded per-session windows, LRU of sessions); the shared library loads from resources or degrades to a no-op. The model reconciliation pass runs only for turn.completed, only when the list is stale AND a step is undecided, under LILY_TODO_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_MS (10s) with kill switch LILY_TODO_MODEL_RECONCILE=0; interrupt/fail paths finalize synchronously as before (turn-orchestrator stop test). Nudge kill switch LILY_TODO_NUDGE=0, cadence LILY_TODO_NUDGE_AFTER.

gates.protects: Any OpenAI-style endpoint can be added and used regardless of which output-limit field it accepts. Every direct request Lily makes (compatibility probe, evidence judge, scheduled-task draft, connectivity diagnostics, vision, the platform gateway's upstream calls) and the engine's configured output limit take their shape from what the server itself answered: `max_tokens` by default, `max_completion_tokens` after a 400 that names the parameter, no temperature after an unsupported_value on it. Nothing is keyed on a model name or host. The learned shape is persisted on the preset (compatibilityProfile.requestShape), handed to the runtime as LILY_MODEL_REQUEST_SHAPE, and remembered per endpoint+model for the process. A rejection for any other reason carries the server's redacted code/param/message to the caller and the UI.
gates.baseline: Reported 2026-09-08: adding an official OpenAI model failed with '保存 API 连接失败' — the probe hard-coded max_tokens, its retry only shrank the number, and the 400 body was reduced to HTTP_400. The same hard-coded field sat in five other call sites and the server gateway; tests passed because every mock accepted anything. Strictly additive: the default shape is byte-identical to the previous requests, adaptation happens only on an explicit 4xx that names a parameter we sent, and is bounded to three lessons per call.
gates.failureFallback: Fail-open by construction: with no rejection nothing changes; a rejection that names no parameter is returned as before (plus structured detail); network errors are structured results, never throws; the engine keeps limit.output unless the learned field is max_completion_tokens AND an output limit is configured. Mutation-verified 2026-09-08 (each fails by name): classifier never adapts; send loop never re-sends; probe forgets the learned shape; profile normalization drops requestShape; engine config ignores the learned shape; probe swallows the server detail; gateway never retries. Output budget follows the same rule: the probe starts at 512 tokens and raises to 4096 only when the server itself reports exhaustion (finish_reason=length with nothing produced — a reasoning model that spent the budget thinking), reusing the working budget for the tool and stream passes; a verdict such as MODEL_TOOL_CALLS_UNAVAILABLE now carries what was observed (content/tool_calls/finish_reason/budget/tool_choice) into the UI. Mutation: removing the escalation fails the strict-endpoint test by name. Surface, too: when the endpoint answers a tools request with "use /v1/responses" (the official API's newer reasoning models refuse function tools on chat/completions and — verified live — also refuse reasoning_effort:'none', so no chat-side setting can help), the probe asks the Responses surface the same question, records api=responses on the preset, and the engine runs that preset on the official SDK, which OpenCode routes through Responses. Verified 2026-09-08 with a real official key: probe ok in 16 s (max_completion_tokens + api=responses, tools via Responses) and a headless engine run executed a real bash tool call. Mutations: classifier ignoring the hint, probe never asking the Responses surface, engine ignoring the learned surface each fail by name. Responses-only models (the codex family answers even a plain chat request with 404 'use the v1/responses endpoint') are covered the same way: the sentence is the lesson with or without tools, and the shared sender then translates the chat-shaped request to the Responses surface (system → instructions, image parts → input_image, tools/tool_choice flattened, limit → max_output_tokens) and normalizes the answer back, so every direct call site stays chat-shaped. Live survey 2026-09-08 with real keys: OpenAI 9 models (4.1-mini plain; 4o-mini/5-mini/5.4-mini/5.5/o4-mini learn max_completion_tokens; 5.3-codex and 6-astra learn api=responses; 5.3-chat-latest is deprecated upstream — catalog staleness, not a shape problem), DeepSeek 4/4 and DashScope 8/8 pass on the default shape untouched. Generic lessons close the long tail without a release: any refused field we sent is dropped (never model/messages/input/stream/tools), 'use X instead' renames any field, a forced tool_choice the gateway refuses falls back to auto, a JSON-schema keyword rejected inside tool parameters (Gemini-style 'Unknown name "additionalProperties"') is stripped at every depth; and for quirks no shipped rule knows the server delivers hints in the signed client config (MODEL_REQUEST_SHAPE_HINTS_JSON or a config profile's models.requestShapeHints → remote-config cache → the classifier), so a new provider is a server setting. A probe rejection that no rule turns into a lesson is reported (host, model, redacted server words, never the key) through the runtime-diagnostics channel so the hint can be written. A Codex/Responses proxy that refuses max_output_tokens (field report 2026-09-09, /codex/v1 gpt-5.3-codex-spark): the learned corrections (drop/rename/strip) now apply to the FINAL wire body after the chat→Responses translation, so a Responses-only field the endpoint refuses is actually dropped — the omit learned from the Responses 400 carries that field name, which the chat body never had; the standalone Responses tool probe drops it too. Mutations: not applying corrections to the translated body, and the tool probe never dropping the field, each fail by name.

gates.protects: A model API key or mail password is never written as plain Base64 by accident. When the OS secure storage is unavailable, saving a NEW secret is refused with SECRET_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (shown to the user in words), the operator can opt in explicitly with LILY_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_SECRETS=1, and operations that merely re-serialize an already stored secret (switch active preset, relabel) keep working by reusing the stored record. Existing plaintext records still read back. Since 2026-09-19 the rule has one home: secret-storage.js is the only module that touches safeStorage, and the device signing key, account refresh token, remote-config cache, license and web credentials go through it — a machine without a keyring keeps working for the run (identity in memory, session in memory, config in memory) but never writes a secret in Base64 without the explicit opt-in.
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-08 protectSecret() silently fell back to Base64 (encrypted:false) in model-presets.js and mail-accounts.js — an encoding presented as storage. Found during the request-shape audit; the collaboration keyring already refused in the same situation, so the repo had the safer precedent.
gates.failureFallback: The read path is unchanged (legacy records decode). The device keypair in service-client.js keeps its fallback because the app cannot start without one — noted, not changed. Test harnesses without Electron opt in explicitly. Mutation-verified 2026-09-08: restoring the silent fallback and removing the stored-record reuse each fail by name.

gates.protects: The runtime identity token's skill authorization scope holds a rich workspace's enabled set, and when it is ever exceeded the failure is legible and actionable.
