The cap (MAX_CAPABILITIES) is a structural sanity bound (256), not a product limit — the token lists every skill whose tools the session may use, so per-turn RELEVANCE is applied at the guidance layer (recommendSkillCapabilityGraph), never by filtering this authorization scope (which would gate off a tool the model reaches for). An over-limit failure names the field that overflowed (activeSkillIds, not capabilities), is its own code (RUNTIME_IDENTITY_TOO_MANY_SKILLS) distinct from a malformed field, reports the count, and the user is told to disable some skills.
gates.baseline: Reported 2026-09-09 (docx audit): a workspace with 76 active skills failed every turn with 'RUNTIME_IDENTITY_FIELD_INVALID: capabilities are invalid' — the cap was 64 (too small for a real workspace), the field was activeSkillIds not capabilities (shared validator, hardcoded message), and the raw code reached the user with nothing to do. The report's 'silently keeps 64, drops 12' was a misreading — the validator THROWS on over-limit, it does not truncate. Verified against the code.
gates.failureFallback: MAX_CAPABILITIES raised 64→256 (256 short ids ≈ a 10KB signed token; zero capability loss, only the previously-failing case now succeeds). Per-turn relevance was already injected at the guidance layer and is unchanged. Message/code hygiene at token issuance plus a friendly ERROR_PATTERNS mapping; the legacy 'capabilities are invalid' string still maps for older/cached errors; a non-array field stays RUNTIME_IDENTITY_FIELD_INVALID, now named. Mutation-verified 2026-09-09: lowering the cap back to 64 fails the 94-skill workspace regression; validating activeSkillIds as 'capabilities' and removing the friendly mapping each fail by name.

gates.protects: A self-configured (BYOK) model that can see images actually receives them. On save/update the endpoint is probed with a tiny image (probeVision), and the detected support is persisted on the preset as capabilities.vision; a manual toggle in the add-model form forces it on when probing is off or a server false-negatives. That flag then reaches every consumer: customPresetRecord carries it so getActivePreset()/listPresetsPublic surface it, the selection catalog and normalizeOption keep it on route.model.capabilities.vision, allowImageFileParts/activePresetSupportsVision route images straight to the model instead of the Qwen-VL translation bridge, and the engine model config sets modalities.input to include 'image'.
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-09 a BYOK model's vision was undetectable and unsettable: presets had no capabilities field, customPresetRecord dropped any capabilities so getActivePreset never saw it, and images from a vision-capable custom model were always forced through the translation bridge — the model 'supported images but we still could not use it'.
gates.failureFallback: Fail-open: no capabilities field means the bridge path is used exactly as before; LILY_PROBE_VISION=0 disables auto-probe and leaves the manual toggle as the sole signal. Mutation-verified 2026-09-09: dropping capabilities from customPresetRecord, skipping the probe-vision persistence, and ignoring the manual toggle each fail the data-flow test by name.

gates.protects: A user with their own OpenAI-compatible image endpoint can actually generate images. The openai adapter (providers/openai.cjs) POSTs /images/generations with the configured model, decodes b64_json into files, accepts a returned url, and self-heals a server that rejects response_format (gpt-image-1) by retrying once without it. A missing key fails loudly with a named error, never a silent no-op. Settings image providers exposes it as a BYOK provider (endpoint+key+model), and media-provider-settings maps that choice to the exact env vars the adapter reads (OPENAI_IMAGE_API_KEY/BASE_URL/MODEL).
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-09 lily-image-generation only had adapters for dashscope/lily/volcengine/kling/minimax/zhipu — there was no OpenAI-compatible image path at all, so a self-configured OpenAI/DALL-E/gpt-image endpoint could not be used for generation ('supported generation but we still could not use it').
gates.failureFallback: Purely additive: a new opt-in BYOK provider plus a new adapter; every existing provider and the service path are untouched, and with no openai key/endpoint configured nothing changes. Mutation-verified 2026-09-09: removing the response_format retry, the b64 decode, and the byokEnv mapping each fail the adapter test by name.

gates.protects: A user generates images with the SAME ChatGPT/Codex account they chat through, and it FOLLOWS the model — no separate standard media provider, no re-entering the key (the relay is not one of our standard services). A custom model flagged capabilities.imageGen routes image generation through its own connection: spawn-env's activePresetImageGenEnv() reads the active preset's base URL, key and model and emits LILY_IMAGE_PROVIDER=codex-relay + CODEX_RELAY_BASE_URL/API_KEY/IMAGE_MODEL (an explicit media-provider choice still wins, being spread after). The codex-relay adapter drives the relay's /chat/completions (which auto-injects the Responses built-in image_generation tool), streams the reply (a non-streamed request 502s behind nginx), buffers the full text, and extracts every data:image data-URI into real files for the normal media pipeline (so a ~2MB image never bloats the transcript/context). A model NOT flagged imageGen emits no image env; missing key/URL or an image-less reply fail loudly.
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-11 image generation had adapters only for dashscope/lily/volcengine/kling/minimax/zhipu/openai, and the openai adapter needed a real /images/generations endpoint + platform key. A ChatGPT-plan Codex relay exposes neither (probed: images route 404) yet its /chat/completions already returns generated images as data:image markdown — there was no Lily path to use it. First shipped as a standard media BYOK provider; changed to model-driven per the design that the relay is non-standard and image generation should follow the active model's own connection.
gates.failureFallback: Additive and opt-in via a per-model toggle (capabilities.imageGen, default off): with no model flagged nothing changes, and an explicit standard media provider still overrides. Streaming avoids the nginx 502; the tier suffix is stripped from the model id. Mutation-verified 2026-09-11: removing the data:image extraction, dropping stream:true, and gating activePresetImageGenEnv on imageGen each fail the test by name.

gates.protects: Adding a model is simpler: paste the API URL + key and Fetch models, and Lily lists what the endpoint actually serves (standard GET /models, OpenAI Bearer or Anthropic x-api-key) so the user picks a real id instead of typing one. Discovery is convenience only and fails SOFT — any error (401/403/404/network/empty) returns { ok:false } and the caller falls back to manual entry, never a thrown error or a blocked save. Capabilities (vision, tool-call, request shape) remain auto-detected by the save-time probe; discovery only fills the model id.
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-11 the custom-model form had no way to enumerate an endpoint's models — the user typed the model id by hand and could only guess what the address served. A server-published catalog existed (models.dev) but nothing queried the user's OWN base URL.
gates.failureFallback: Purely additive: a new opt-in Fetch-models button + discovery module; the manual model-id field is unchanged and remains the fallback whenever discovery fails. Mutation-verified 2026-09-11: making discovery throw instead of returning ok:false, and dropping the auth header, each fail the test by name. Verified live against the real relay (37 models).

gates.protects: 智能体 (agents) bind Lily's existing behaviour dimensions — role card, skills, knowledge packs, autonomy, model, tool policy, automations — to a conversation as HOST configuration, applied through the existing per-dimension setters, with an inert natural-language drafting tool and an official catalog that replaces the hard-coded legal-counsel knowledge coupling with data.
gates.baseline: Sessions without an agent binding behave exactly as before: same skill resolution, permission mode, model selection, character binding, knowledge preparation (the official legal role still requires the legal pack) and broker tool list plus lily_agent_draft. Role cards remain a lower-authority narrative suffix; the role activation contract is untouched.
gates.failureFallback: Every dimension applies independently and fails open to today's default with a named reason in the activation receipt; cold dimensions (model, tools.disallow) degrade to inherit beyond the serve fork budget; deactivate restores the exact pre-activation snapshot; unknown knowledge packs are reported by id; the kill switch LILY_AGENTS=0 hides the library, refuses activation and makes every agent-derived policy read inactive while stored bindings stay readable.

gates.protects: A turn's artifact list shows the files the user asked for, not the working material the turn created on the way there.
gates.baseline: Every produced path is still discovered, registered and downloadable; only what the turn presents as a deliverable is narrowed.
gates.failureFallback: If narrowing would leave nothing, the working material is kept and shown compact, so the list is never emptied.

gates.protects: A drawn PDF keeps its Chinese text: the CJK font handed to the Python runtime is one ReportLab can actually embed.
gates.baseline: Font preference order is unchanged, and an unreadable probe is no opinion rather than a rejection.
gates.failureFallback: When nothing embeddable exists the first font that merely exists is still returned, exactly as before the probe existed; with no CJK font at all the skill falls open to Helvetica.

gates.protects: An empty search result over a Word/Excel/PowerPoint/PDF file never masquerades as 'the document does not contain that'.
gates.baseline: Metadata chunks, filesIndexed counts and coverage are unchanged; content extraction is opt-in and every background/main-process caller keeps the old behaviour.
gates.failureFallback: Extraction is bounded by file size, per-file timeout, run file count and run wall clock, and every failure falls open to the metadata chunk plus a named reason in metadataOnly. LILY_INDEX_DOCUMENT_CONTENT=0 restores the previous behaviour exactly.

gates.protects: A healthy Web Automation pack makes browser tools actually usable, and the Playwright module tree always matches the browsers beside it.
gates.baseline: A bundled Node interpreter still wins over the app binary, and a build with neither a pack nor a bundled runtime stays a clean no-op.
gates.failureFallback: No pack and no bundled playwright means no playwright MCP server at all, the same silent no-op as before.

gates.protects: A delivered Office document is whole: a chart is not split across a page break, a document title survives conversion, and a chart image can actually be produced.
gates.baseline: Print setup is additive polish that never fails a workbook, and the chart renderer is a declared runtime dependency checked at build time.
gates.failureFallback: style_xlsx_print never raises and returns an empty list for anything that is not a workbook; a runtime without matplotlib degrades to the workbook's own native chart.

gates.protects: A LibreOffice conversion never reports success without producing a file.
gates.baseline: Every conversion that worked before still works, through the same single code path; the renderer keeps its behaviour.
gates.failureFallback: A conversion that produces nothing raises with LibreOffice's own stderr instead of returning a path that does not exist.

gates.protects: A file tool's result is bounded by BYTES, so a few very long lines cannot flood the model's context.
gates.baseline: Results that already fit keep their exact previous shape, with no new fields and no changed coverage.
gates.failureFallback: A cut is always reported and resumable (truncatedBytes + nextLine), never silent, and never returns nothing — a single oversized line is cut mid-line on a character boundary.

gates.protects: A file whose bytes contradict its extension is flagged before anything trusts the type.
gates.baseline: `kind` stays extension-derived — indexing, extraction routing and the binary guards are unchanged; the signature result is additive.
gates.failureFallback: An unreadable header, an unchecked extension, or bytes that declare no format produce no advisory at all rather than a false accusation.

gates.protects: A Chinese value written into a PDF form is drawn correctly by every reader: the fill writes the field's appearance with an embedded CJK font subset and verifies the flattened field box reads back as the value; the verification renderer draws form fields.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-29: pypdf's Helvetica appearance held a literal '??????' (our preview, Firefox, printing drew it; pdfium and macOS Preview redrew), the ink check passed it, and the renderer drew filled fields blank. A Latin-only fill is unchanged.
gates.failureFallback: No usable CJK font, or a value the font cannot fully draw: the field is left to the viewer with /NeedAppearances on and listed in leftToViewer, verified false; when pdfium is unavailable the old pixel check runs and says so. Mutation-verified: no embedding, ink-only verification, still asking viewers to redraw and a renderer without forms each fail by name.

gates.protects: The bundled image library can still save a multi-page PDF by filename, so an image-to-PDF path cannot break on a dependency bump.
gates.baseline: Build-time only; no runtime behaviour changes.
gates.failureFallback: The bundle verifier warns (or fails under strict smoke) with the fix named, instead of the defect reaching users.

gates.protects: A contract only names a helper the agent can actually reach in the RUNNING build, and only promises functions that helper really defines.
gates.baseline: The helpers and their contents are unchanged; what changes is that the path is absolute and exported instead of repo-relative.
gates.failureFallback: If the runtime-scripts directory cannot be resolved the variable is simply absent, and a skill script falls back to its previous relative lookup.

gates.protects: A managed job's stderr shows what the JOB wrote, so a successful job is not mistaken for a failed one.
gates.baseline: The stderr log file is never rewritten, real job output is never filtered, and a job that truly failed still reads as failed.
gates.failureFallback: Only the host logger's own line format matches; anything else is passed through untouched, and what was removed is reported alongside.

gates.protects: A job that exits 0 having processed nothing is distinguishable from one that did the work.
gates.baseline: Additive fields only; no job status, exit code or existing field changes, and nothing calls a success a failure.
gates.failureFallback: The fields state what was OBSERVED (a positive progress count, a percent, or output files) and never infer a verdict, so a legitimately fast job is not accused.

gates.protects: A set of PDFs exported from one source can be made to embed the same CJK font instead of a different substitute per format.
gates.baseline: The default declared family is unchanged, so an Office file delivered to a Windows reader still names Microsoft YaHei.
gates.failureFallback: When the installed font set cannot be read the preferred family is returned unchanged, which is exactly the previous behaviour.

gates.protects: Every piece of Chinese text in a generated document uses the font that was set for it, including headings and native chart labels.
gates.baseline: Runs and styles are set exactly as before; the theme reference is removed and the theme and chart parts are filled in addition, never instead.
gates.failureFallback: A theme or chart part that cannot be edited is skipped and the document still authors and saves; the previous behaviour is the floor.

gates.protects: A Python process gets the dependency set it was meant to have: the declared runtime, plus at most the one pack that is actually doing the work.
gates.baseline: Pack engines keep working — the document extractor attaches the pro-pdf engine exactly when the caller selects it, and every pack stays reachable through its own environment.
gates.failureFallback: An unknown or uninstalled pack contributes nothing rather than failing the call, and LILY_RUNTIME_PACK_GLOBAL_PYTHONPATH=1 restores the previous global behaviour exactly.

gates.protects: OCR reads a scan whatever colour space it arrived in, and an empty result from a page that plainly has ink is reported rather than passed off as 'no text here'.
gates.baseline: Images that already read correctly are unchanged; the PDF page path keeps its existing normalisation.
gates.failureFallback: If the image cannot be opened for normalisation, OCR still reads the file directly exactly as before; a genuinely blank image produces no warning.

gates.protects: A failed extraction names a cause the caller can act on instead of an empty exception message.
gates.baseline: The original exception type and message are preserved verbatim; the diagnosis is an added field.
gates.failureFallback: An unrecognised cause adds nothing at all, so corruption is never mislabelled as encryption.

gates.protects: A text file larger than the index cap yields searchable evidence from its head instead of no evidence at all, and says how much was covered.
gates.baseline: Files within the cap are indexed byte-for-byte as before, with unchanged coverage.
gates.failureFallback: Binary content is still refused, now under its own reason so 'too large' and 'binary' are distinguishable, and the truncation is reported with the bytes indexed and what to do about it.

gates.protects: A turn whose dispatch outcome is unknown is announced once, not once per app restart for the rest of the conversation's life.
gates.baseline: The notice itself, its wording, and the list the user sees are unchanged; a genuinely new unknown outcome is still announced immediately.
gates.failureFallback: If the durable transition cannot be written the notice is still emitted, which is exactly the previous behaviour — bookkeeping never silences a warning.

gates.protects: Reopening a conversation shows a turn's ANSWER in the answer slot, with the narration written while working kept where it belongs.
gates.baseline: The full stream is still stored and still shown; only which part lands in which slot changes, and the answer text is passed through byte-identical.
gates.failureFallback: A record saved before the boundary existed renders exactly as it does today, and a real timeline always wins over the reconstruction.

gates.protects: A prompt the platform sends to itself never reads as the user's, and a self-check's answer never reads as the assistant volunteering. Provenance is stamped where the platform composes the prompt, not recognised downstream from its wording.
gates.baseline: The prompt text the model receives is unchanged apart from the tag, and every prompt recognised before is still recognised — including history written before the tag existed.
gates.failureFallback: An untagged or unknown-kind prompt falls back to the safe reading (self_check), and a recovery prompt's ANSWER is always kept because it is the work the user asked for. The seam defaults to recovery, so a new nudge added without thinking about kinds hides only the platform's question. Text the user typed — the pending payload, a steer, and the retries that re-deliver the same request after an engine rebuild — never passes through the seam and is never stamped, so a user's own message can never be hidden from their conversation.

gates.protects: A schema bump cannot make the application look wrong, and cannot make it work at startup in order to look right. Records are displayed at the current artifact schema whether or not the background pass has reached them, and that pass — still bounded and resumable — is now only a cache warm-up.
gates.baseline: Every record still reaches the same re-derived state it would have reached before — the same derivation over the same messages, only sliced; nothing is skipped silently and nothing is derived twice. Proven, not assumed: with the derived fields stripped from two copies of one real 1506-message database, the whole-session pass and the sliced pass interrupted twice both rewrote 557 records and every stored envelope is byte-for-byte identical. No prompt, skill, guide, tool or model path is touched, and no consumer reads the schema versions, so a session left half-enriched by a restart displays exactly as a pre-backfill one did. Display no longer depends on the migration at all: the conversation read path re-derives a stale record in memory before returning it (measured on a real database: 14 ms for a 50-record page, against 205 ms to write those records back, which is why only persistence is deferred). Proven end to end — with every derived field stripped from a real database and the background pass never run, an opened page returned 24 of 24 records at the current schema while the database still held 0 upgraded.
gates.failureFallback: Every failure path lands on the same baseline — records displayed from their stored artifacts, which is what shipped before any backfill existed: the kill switch LILY_SESSION_ENRICHMENT=0 does no enrichment at all; a store without the bounded read does none either, rather than an unbounded one; missing schema versions refuse to build or delete a single key, because every key embeds them and a missing one would sweep the live cursors and re-queue everything from zero; a record that cannot be read or written is skipped and counted, never allowed to cost its session the rest of its history; a slice that cannot advance its cursor stops that session unflagged instead of re-reading the same rows forever; and a workspace-less session waits for a launch that knows its project.

gates.protects: The launch gate blocks on the message database's page-by-page verification only when there is reason to doubt the file, so a large history does not cost seconds of staring at a check screen on every cold launch.
gates.baseline: Verification coverage per launch is unchanged — the full PRAGMA integrity_check still runs every launch, in the background once the window is open, and its result is persisted. The fast admission is the SAME decision minus that one scan: header, schema, hot-journal rollback, restore-receipt resume and the message/session counts are all still made before the app opens, and a probe and a full inspect return identical results on a healthy database.
gates.failureFallback: Every uncertainty answers "verify": a missing, truncated, corrupt or wrong-version marker, a previous run that never reached before-quit (crash, force quit, power loss), a background verification that failed or never finished, and the kill switch LILY_STARTUP_FAST_ADMIT=0 all restore the old always-blocking gate. A background failure is recorded so the next launch blocks and reaches the repair flow with its candidates.

gates.protects: A finished answer stays finished and a running one shows once: a turn occupies exactly one card in the conversation, whatever sequence of live events, commits, re-renders, pagination passes or turn handovers led there.
gates.baseline: Nothing is suppressed, and there is no second index of what is live: the list itself is both the display and the record, since is-live/is-sealed are toggled from the view model on every render. Identity decides placement, not content — an article carrying a turn id replaces the one already standing for that turn, in place, keeping position and every block of the newest render. Articles without a turn id — notices, scheduled drafts, binding cards — are never reconciled, and reconciliation is scoped to one session's list.
gates.failureFallback: Identity is (turn id AND assistant-turn-article), so the user's own bubble — which carries the same turn id for the minimap — is never mistaken for the answer. An article with no turn id has no identity and is appended as before; a null list or article returns null instead of throwing inside a render pass; a live shell is refused over any committed card for the same turn but never the reverse, so an answer is never replaced by an emptier view of itself. There is no runtime repair pass: a source rule in the test keeps every producer of a turn article going through the mount point, so a duplicate cannot be created rather than being tidied up afterwards.

gates.protects: Content Lily removes from history before a model call can never be mistaken for the real thing: a file body the model may be asked to reproduce is replaced by a pointer to it, never by an excerpt, and every placeholder says what was removed, where the real content is, and what to do about it.
gates.baseline: Nothing the model needs is lost. Referential content - a tool output, an earlier answer - is still excerpted head+tail, because the model reasons about it and some text beats none; only content it may be asked to REPRODUCE is replaced whole. The real content is on disk and the marker names the path, so a re-read restores everything. The pointer is also far smaller than the excerpt it replaces, which leaves context budget for parts still worth keeping.
gates.failureFallback: Recognition is anchored at the start of a body, so a real file that merely quotes a marker is never refused; a marker with no path still tells the model to read the file before rewriting; an unknown or legacy marker is still recognised, because every sentence written before this contract is listed. If the contract module cannot be loaded, the guards fail open exactly as before - they never throw and never break a turn.

gates.protects: When the active model cannot read images, Lily's own vision bridge still delivers the picture's content to it: the reply text is extracted once, at the transport seam, from choices[0].message.content, and every caller (chat attachments, document-embedded images) reads it there. An empty reply names the server's finish reason, and the user-facing 'image skipped' notice carries the bridge's actual reason instead of a bare chip.
gates.baseline: Image questions to DeepSeek and other text-only models are answered from the vision model's description, exactly as before the 2026-09-08 request-shape refactor. The bridge is exercised end-to-end through the real transport with only fetch stubbed, so a change to what the transport returns can no longer stay invisible behind tests that inject the translate function.
gates.failureFallback: A vision reply that is genuinely empty still fails the image with a reason (content_filter, length) rather than a generic sentence; the chip still says the image was skipped and the answering model still receives the fallback context naming the file. Transport errors keep their HTTP status. Nothing about which model is used, or the key resolution order, changes.

gates.protects: A runner the orchestrator has claimed for a turn is never terminated under that turn by a configuration change. The runner owns one idleness predicate (alive, not busy, not claimed), every idle-termination path asks it, and the claim is the turn's own liveness rather than a flag that must be released. A dispatch failure with no engine at all confirms immediately instead of waiting out the SSE grace window.
gates.baseline: Every configuration change still reaches every idle runner exactly as before: a runner with no turn in flight is terminated on settings save, login, permission-mode change, skill sync and runtime-pack refresh. A claimed runner receives the same change at its next send, because ensureProcess already recycles on a model/tool config change. Genuinely idle runners, dead runners and the pre-turn refresh for the current turn behave identically to before.
gates.failureFallback: A claim predicate that throws cannot hold a claim, so the runner reads as idle (the old behaviour). A stand-in runner without isIdle gets the pre-reservation baseline. If the claim were somehow never made, the turn is exactly as exposed as before and the rescue table still retries RUNNER_TERMINATED. Busy runners are never terminated by a skill change any more — previously a skill toggle could kill an in-flight turn.

gates.protects: Every chat-completion reply is read through one module: the assistant text (string or content parts), reasoning, tool calls, finish reason, and whether the reply is a completion at all. A probe judges the reply, never the HTTP status, so a gateway that answers 200 with an HTML error page or an error envelope is not mistaken for a model that read the image.
gates.baseline: Every consumer reads exactly what it read before, in every shape it handled before, plus the shapes it mishandled (content-part arrays in the compatibility probe). The vision probe still returns true for a 200 completion and false for a 4xx that names images or for a network failure; the only change is that a 200 without a completion is now false instead of true.
gates.failureFallback: A reply that cannot be read yields '' / [] / false, never a throw; callers keep their own empty-handling. If the seam module failed to load the callers would fail at require time in tests, not silently at runtime. A source-scan rule forbids reading choices[0] by hand anywhere else, so a new caller cannot regress to a status-code verdict unnoticed.

gates.protects: Every JSON state file the app keeps is written atomically through json-file.js: the bytes land in a temporary file next to the target and are renamed over it, so a crash, kill or power cut mid-write can never leave a truncated file that reads back as empty. Reading never throws; a missing or malformed file is the caller's fallback.
gates.baseline: Every file has exactly the bytes its writer produced before (indent, trailing newline, owner-only mode preserved per call site); readers are unchanged; MCP servers and long-task workers use the same dependency-free module from their own processes. Transient Windows rename locks are retried briefly, as the session index already did.
gates.failureFallback: A write that fails leaves the previous file intact and no temporary behind; the error reaches the caller exactly as a failed writeFileSync did. A source-scan rule forbids a second implementation (two documented exceptions: a create-only marker with flag wx, and a store with an injected fs), so no new state file can regress to a plain write unnoticed.

A format added once is known everywhere; a file is never one kind in one module and another kind in the next.

gates.protects: A turn's record holds only the tools that turn ran. The engine's end-of-turn context pruning republishes EARLIER turns' tool parts (marked state.time.compacted); the reducer treats one it never saw this turn as bookkeeping, not a new step — so evidence counts, side-effect and progress decisions, and the plan card all describe this turn.
gates.baseline: A tool part seen running this turn reports started/done exactly as before, and its later pruning reports nothing new.
gates.failureFallback: A live tool never carries the compacted marker, so nothing this turn ran can be dropped; a pruned part met first here is the previous turn's and is ignored.

gates.protects: The per-turn process-job scope is issued with the turn's identity on dispatch and attached to every lily_process_jobs call by the engine plugin (a subagent's child session inherits it through its parent); the model never copies the token and the prompt no longer carries it.
gates.baseline: Scope semantics are unchanged: a session may only touch its own turn's jobs, verified with the same secret. With no grant for the session (or LILY_PROCESS_JOB_SCOPE_INJECT=0) the call is left exactly as the model made it and the prompt carries the token as before.
gates.failureFallback: Issuance failure never fails the identity grant; the previous prompt-carried route remains.

gates.protects: A background job's wake brings the conversation an outcome it has not read: an outcome already returned through job_status/job_logs retires the wake silently; a running or queued turn makes the wake wait (never behind the user's own messages, spending no continuation budget); wakes of one turn are delivered as one turn; a turn that already gave its final answer is asked for a brief report, not resumed.
gates.baseline: A job that finishes while the session is idle wakes it as before; failure and unknown outcomes still wake; the continuation budget, ownership and scope checks are unchanged.
gates.failureFallback: Without an orchestrator snapshot the wake is delivered as before; a handler that does not speak for siblings sees each delivered on its own; a database from before the observation column gains it on open.

gates.protects: A changed skill reaches the machines that installed it. A published version names exactly one pack: the client reinstalls a service-managed skill whose registry pack digest differs from the one it installed, even at the same version; the publisher refuses to upload a different pack under a version the server already holds (--bump-changed raises the patch version, manifest and registry, and restamps); the server answers 409 SKILL_VERSION_IMMUTABLE to the same. A changed pack means changed files: packs zip reproducibly (folder entries pinned like files), and when an archive hash differs from the published one the published pack is fetched and compared by content digest — same files are skipped, never refused or re-uploaded; an unreadable published pack counts as changed.
gates.baseline: A higher version still updates exactly as before; metadata-only republishes (same digest) stay allowed; user-installed and GitHub-sourced skills keep version rules.
gates.failureFallback: A pack without a recorded digest (bundled, GitHub) is judged by version alone; a failed reinstall retries on the next sync and never downgrades.

gates.protects: The engine offers the model Lily's skills only: the shared serve denies the engine's native skill tool (Lily skills reach the model through AGENT.md and the capability graph) and starts with the scan of ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills off.
gates.baseline: Lily's catalog and platform guides are delivered exactly as before; per-session permission modes already denied the tool.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_ENGINE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1 restores the scan.

gates.protects: The skill usage audit measures the capability router's actual recommendation for the turn (carried on the engine trace), records guides the model read without a recommendation, and the report counts both — so router precision and blind spots are measured, not guessed. The recommendation itself is actionable: each guide is the installed copy the AGENT.md catalog lists, as an absolute path, and a recovery turn is routed on the user's request it carries rather than on the platform's correction.
gates.baseline: A turn with no routing keeps the previous word-overlap candidates; older audits aggregate as before.
gates.failureFallback: Any audit failure leaves the record without an audit, as before; the audit is advisory and never gates a turn.

gates.protects: When the capability router has a rule-level best match (score >= 120), the turn says so as an instruction: read that guide completely before acting, or say in one line why it does not fit — Codex's trigger rule applied to Lily's router. Every prompt's capability catalog also asks the model to name the guide it follows and explain skipping a clear match (zh-CN/en/ar).
gates.baseline: The recommendation listing is unchanged; the directive's characters are granted on top of the capability-context budget, so no skill or route line kept before is displaced; keyword-hint matches (below 120) and chat get no directive.
gates.failureFallback: The guide body is never injected (the router misfires even at high scores), so a wrong best match costs one declinable line; any failure returns no directive; LILY_SKILL_BEST_MATCH_DIRECTIVE=0 restores the listing alone. Since 2026-09-29 skill routing runs in shadow by default (gate skill-routing-shadow): the listing and this directive appear only with LILY_SKILL_ROUTING_SHADOW=0; the catalog's name-the-guide / explain-a-skip rule still applies every turn.

gates.protects: A subagent (and the main turn) is not reported failed for a tool failure it RECOVERED from. One shared organ (tool-completion-status.partitionToolCompletion) classifies tools recovery-aware: a failed tool becomes 'recovered' once a later same-name tool succeeds. The subagent projection derives its failed set through it (refreshSubagentPhase), an authoritative done wins over a stray unrecovered failure, and a single child tool failure never flips the whole subagent's status to failed — only an engine error (kind:error) or the parent task tool (syncFromTool) is authoritative. The incomplete-turn card lists still-running tools under a distinct '运行中未结束' label, never '失败'.
gates.baseline: Before 2026-09-27 the subagent projection marked the whole subtask failed on ANY failed tool (refreshSubagentPhase: `failedTools.length`; applyEvent flipped status to failed on one failed tool), with no recovery-awareness — so a no-match grep (exit 1) or a first-try command the subagent then recovered showed the subtask 失败 and counted in 'N 个子任务失败'. The main turn had adopted recovery-awareness on 2026-09-02 (fccfb9f3) but the subagent path was never brought in line. The incomplete-turn card also listed still-running tools under '未完成或失败的子任务', so a long background poll (Start-Sleep) read as a failed subtask.
gates.failureFallback: Display/telemetry honesty only, fail-open: authoritative failures (engine error, parent task tool failed) still surface; genuine unrecovered failures still show. Mutation-verified 2026-09-27: reverting refreshSubagentPhase to the naive filter, reverting applyEvent to flip status on a lone failed tool, and merging running back into the failed card label each fail a test by name.

gates.protects: A custom model's context window is known: a preset carries it (settings field, accepts 256k/1m/100万) into LILY_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS; a window read from the endpoint's listing or from an overflow error naming the limit is learned, kept on disk per endpoint+model, and found under any spelling of the endpoint; the compaction budget, the engine model limit and the context-window guard all read the same window.
gates.baseline: An operator-delivered window still wins; with nothing configured, learned or catalogued the window is reported unknown (context-window-honest); a listing without the field or an error without a limit teaches nothing.
gates.failureFallback: Without a writable user-data directory learned windows stay in memory, as before; a failing store read or write is logged and changes nothing else.

gates.protects: Auto mode uses ONLY the models the user selected, prefers the ones that currently work, and fails over within that pool instead of dying on one bad model. One organ holds model health: model-availability (the picker's existing silent-model marks) now also records model-attributable turn failures, with an escalating backoff (90s → 5m → 15m → 30m) kept in a failure history that outlives each mark, deduped against the first-response watchdog for the same event, and cleared on the model's next clean success. resolveTurnModel annotates routing options with those marks; routeTurn (auto branch only) prefers unmarked selected models and honors an explicit avoidModelIds, strictly inside autoModelIds and never emptying the pool. A failed auto turn fails over by re-running with the escaped model named explicitly in avoidModelIds (flowing through the queue whitelist and the retry pin-escape), hard-bounded per session (3 per 10 min), stopping if an escaped model fails again, only on side-effect-free turns, only while a selected unmarked alternative exists, never after the user switched to manual, and its notice is emitted against the retry turn. Retries/continuations drop the source-turn pin when that model is marked, avoided, or (auto) deselected; a manual pick is never overridden. The picker lists selected models first (order frozen while open) and badges recently failed models. A failed engine message keeps its error envelope (name / HTTP status / retryability, never the body) through history recovery, so a provider 429 whose message is literally "Error" is classified RATE_LIMITED by the one runner-failure classifier — feeding both the mark/failover and an honest message — instead of surfacing "Assistant engine returned failure: Error".
gates.baseline: 2026-09-27 field case: auto pool [claude, deepseek]; claude's upstream went silent/429. Routing had no health input (availability marks were UI-only and normalizeOption dropped them), so claude kept being picked; the first failover build re-sent 13 times in 20 minutes to claude because the retry re-pinned the source turn's model and the loop bound relied on routing avoiding the failed model; after the 5-minute mark expired a fresh turn picked claude again. The picker listed models in catalog order, so the selected claude sat below the fold and the user believed only deepseek was selected. The 8 subagents themselves all completed on the selected deepseek — the failures were parent-turn routing.
gates.failureFallback: Advisory + fail-open; kill switch LILY_MODEL_HEALTH_ROUTING=0 restores mark-blind routing and disables failover. Marks never remove a model the user can pick manually, and an all-marked pool still routes. Mutation-verified 2026-09-27: retry without explicit avoid, no re-escape stop, failover after a manual switch, failover target outside the pool, routing ignoring marks, normalizeOption dropping the mark, no escalating history, retry re-pinning an avoided model, and the picker not sorting selected-first each fail a test by name.

gates.protects: The message the model is being asked to answer (the latest user message with non-synthetic text) reaches it whole: the context-window guard's budget pass never excerpts it, so a question layered between platform context and the attachment note cannot be cut out by head+tail trimming.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-27 field case: a legal knowledge-base question in a long release session over the guard budget was trimmed to head+tail; the model reasoned there was no user request and resumed the previous task.
gates.failureFallback: History and this turn's tool outputs are still bounded; the per-part hard cap still applies to a pathological single message, so the deadlock guard is unchanged. Kill switch LILY_CONTEXT_GUARD=0 unchanged. Mutation-verified: removing the exemption fails the field-shape test.

gates.protects: The test runner never passes an inherited LILY_USER_DATA_DIR (Lily's agent shell carries the live directory): Node tests run without it, Electron tests always get a throwaway directory, a deliberate one is LILY_TEST_USER_DATA_DIR.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-27: a suite run from a Lily conversation wrote example.com fixture windows into the live model-context-windows.json because the runner skipped isolation whenever LILY_USER_DATA_DIR was set.
gates.failureFallback: Without an inherited variable Node commands run with an unchanged environment; if a temp directory cannot be made an Electron test gets a fixed temp path and the failure is printed. Mutation-verified: the old runner fails the test.

gates.protects: A model's context window is configured, learned from its endpoint (listing, an overflow naming the limit, or the largest accepted request as a rising ceiling), catalogued by exact model id — or reported unknown, never guessed. With an unknown window no pressure compaction is invented and the context-window guard bounds single oversized parts only. With a known one the guard measures the real input limit against the engine's reported usage and trims just enough, never the current request. An overflow the engine compacts itself is not a turn failure; a failed compaction is reported as an overflow; a visible overflow teaches the window, is recorded so the next turn compacts first, keeps the conversation, and is retried once on a rebuilt runner. Settings show the effective window and its source and round-trip every capability.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-27: 573 of 595 compaction decisions and every guard budget used a hardcoded 120,000; a 1M model's long session was trimmed on every call down to the user's question (answered with the previous task); engine-side overflow compaction was reported as a failure; visible overflows discarded the engine session; editing a preset cleared its window and imageGen.
gates.failureFallback: Kill switch LILY_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_RECOVERY=0 restores the previous overflow handling; a second overflow nothing compacted falls back to a fresh engine session (the previous behaviour); every failure to learn, record or check is logged and fails open. Mutation-verified 2026-09-27: ten mutations (guard fallback budget, estimate over report, no engine-overflow absorb, dropped resume, no retry, no forced compaction, catalog by name, silent compaction failure, vision-only public capabilities, floor instead of bisection) each fail a named test.

gates.protects: Lossy context operations happen only under MEASURED pressure, as in the engine, Claude Code and Codex CLI: background and pre-turn compaction fire when a known window is crossed or the provider reported an overflow, never on turn count; an unknown window is left to the engine's own overflow compaction. Tool-output prune stays at the engine default (off) — trimming under pressure belongs to context-window-guard, which bounds a per-request copy and never rewrites history.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: background compaction fired on 24 turns alone (89 times in one field log), summarizing a 1M-window session at 5% use down to its last two turns every 20 minutes; Lily enabled prune (engine default off), which after every turn permanently erased tool outputs older than two turns beyond the newest 40k tokens whatever the window — including skill guides read through `read`, since the only tool prune protects (native skill) is denied.
gates.failureFallback: LILY_OPENCODE_PRUNE=1 restores prune. Real pressure and provider overflow still compact natively (DeepSeek, compactBoundary and failure rate-limit paths are driven by real pressure in the tests). Legacy sessions already pruned keep being restored by compaction-continuity. Mutation-verified 2026-09-28: re-adding the turn-count branch fails three tests by name; re-enabling prune fails the config test.

gates.protects: The host never asserts that a turn is a new task on wording it did not recognise. With earlier work and no explicit relation the intent relation is `unspecified`: the model judges it from the conversation, no isolation instruction is injected, and no memory (session summary, evidence gaps, compaction state) is withheld. Only an explicit new-task phrase yields `new`, which keeps the isolation instruction and memory withholding. Either way separate work may not overwrite or repurpose an earlier task's deliverables. Refinement is only a verb acting on the previous result or lifting its constraint (改成/换成/再加/加上/去掉/再详细/also add/change it, 现在可以联网搜索); modality and generic openers (不要/必须/只要/重点/按/补充, a bare 现在可以, 不是…而是) are not a relation, and earlier work is any assistant turn in the conversation, not only a stored contract snapshot.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: any phrasing the continuation regexes missed (e.g. 用 Python 实现第二个方案) defaulted to `new`, which told the model prior conversation was background only and dropped compaction state, so a compacted session lost its own history on an ordinary follow-up. The 2026-08-13 protection (a new request must not modify an earlier task's output directory) is preserved.
gates.failureFallback: `unspecified` is not inherited, exactly like the old default, so the deliverable gate never demands an earlier task's files; source-resolution guidance and procedure cards treat it as not inherited (unchanged). Mutation-verified 2026-09-28: fallback back to `new`, withholding memory for `unspecified`, and isolating `unspecified` each fail by name.

gates.protects: Plan mode can look at the workspace with the shell, as the engine plan agent and Claude Code plan mode can: a provably read-only command (every segment a known read-only program without its writing or executing flags, no redirection, substitution, backgrounding or variable assignment) runs; anything else asks the user; edits stay denied.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: plan mode denied every bash command, so a plan could not even run ls, git log or rg; with WebFetch also denied it had no way to investigate beyond the read tool.
gates.failureFallback: Any doubt answers not-read-only and ASKS; nothing unknown is auto-allowed. Unattended turns still turn ask into deny; the catastrophic backstop and edit denial are unchanged. Mutation-verified: dropping the syntax check, dropping the flag check, denying shell again and allowing all shell each fail by name.

gates.protects: Engine-native capabilities Lily has no better replacement for stay on: the engine webfetch (local fetch, no key, bounded, format-aware; the webfetch skill is its fallback), the engine tool-output truncation (every built-in, plugin and MCP result, 50 KB / 2000 lines, full text saved with a grep/page hint), and the engine external_directory allow-list for its own truncation, tmp and skill directories.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: WebFetch was still denied from the Claude Code era (whose WebFetch preflights domains against Anthropic, unreachable from mainland China); a Lily plugin re-truncated tool output to 32k chars head+tail, tighter than the engine and ahead of it on MCP results; and a plain external_directory ask (last rule wins) overrode the engine allow-list, so reading the full output the engine saved needed a permission card and plan mode could not read it.
gates.failureFallback: WebSearch stays Lily's own (the engine's needs Exa). Every other outside path still asks through the engine default and the host policy. Old histories keep their large tool output markers recognised by lib/history-elision.cjs. Mutation-verified: re-denying WebFetch and re-adding the external_directory override each fail by name.

gates.protects: Context trimming and paste staging follow THIS turn's model window. The guard measures each turn against the budget of the model it runs on (every configured model's own budget, from the engine config limit.context), trims only when the request would not fit, and only as far as needed; single oversized parts are capped only when the window is unknown. A paste is inlined while it takes at most a quarter of the model's usable input, as Claude Code and Codex CLI send it, and staged for retrieval beyond that.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: every history part over 48k chars lost its middle whatever the window (a report the user then asked to revise); the budget was the serve's start-up model even when auto mode routed a turn elsewhere; under pressure parts were cut to 48k even when far less trimming fitted; and any paste over 40k chars was staged, so a 1M-window model saw a 6,000-char preview of a 50k-char contract.
gates.failureFallback: Unknown window: the previous per-part cap and 40k-char staging threshold. Lite-graded models keep the previous staging threshold and enforced retrieval; an operator LILY_LARGE_INPUT_STAGE_CHARS still wins; a model missing from the budget map uses the serve budget. Kill switches LILY_CONTEXT_GUARD=0 and LILY_LARGE_INPUT_STAGE=0 unchanged. Mutation-verified: pass 1 always, serve-wide budget, a 48k search ceiling, a fixed staging threshold and ignoring lite each fail by name.

gates.protects: An answer over a PARTIALLY read source is never replaced: it stands with a scope note that is true whatever the answer claimed (only the read part is grounded; anything about the unread part, a claim of completeness included, is unverified). Only an answer over a source nothing was read from is replaced, since every content claim there is fabricated by construction.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: a prose regex (完整展示, 全部价格, entire document…) decided an answer overclaimed and replaced the WHOLE answer with a template, discarding the real analysis of the pages that were read, against the delivered-content-is-never-zero invariant (evidence-risk-tiers).
gates.failureFallback: The scope note keeps the wording the evidence gate recognises as a partial-scope disclosure; the unread-attachment replacement and the source-coverage retry are unchanged. Mutation-verified: putting a regex-driven replacement back fails test-source-coverage-recovery by name.

gates.protects: Streaming usage — what the engine measures overflow and compaction pressure with — is on for every OpenAI-compatible endpoint the compatibility probe VERIFIED: it accepted stream_options.include_usage, returned usage and kept every chunk's choices. It is off only where that was not verified.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: includeUsage was false for every OpenAI-compatible endpoint because some vLLM deployments send a usage chunk without choices, which the engine's AI SDK (2.0.41 still requires choices) rejects mid-turn; that blinded overflow detection and every pressure measurement on every such model.
gates.failureFallback: The probe's usage step can never fail a model the plain stream passes: anything short of verification re-sends the stream exactly as before and records nothing. Unverified and pre-existing presets keep usage off (the previous behaviour); LILY_PROBE_STREAM_USAGE=0 skips the step. Mutation-verified: ignoring choiceless chunks, turning usage on unconditionally and keeping it off unconditionally each fail by name.

gates.protects: A provider that answers 429/5xx is not a silent model: while the engine has scheduled a retry, the first-response window is measured from that scheduled attempt, so only silence after it ends the turn as MODEL_NO_RESPONSE and marks the model silent.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: the engine's session.status retry (with the provider's retry-after or its own backoff) was reduced as no progress, so 90s into a rate-limited turn the fuse ended it as MODEL_NO_RESPONSE and marked the model silent, steering auto mode away from a model that was only rate-limited.
gates.failureFallback: Unchanged for a model that is genuinely silent (no retry scheduled), for compaction, pending cards and tool leases; a stale retry status cannot defer forever because the window runs from the scheduled attempt; an engine that gives up ends the turn itself with the provider's real error. LILY_OPENCODE_FIRST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS still tunes or disables the fuse. Mutation-verified: ignoring the retry fails by name. Only a retry scheduled within one no-progress window is followed; a farther retry-after (an exhausted quota) is treated as an outage and the turn ends as before, so auto mode can fail over.

gates.protects: The explore subagent keeps the engine's specialist prompt (glob/grep/read routing, thoroughness levels, never modify the user's system) and its read-only permission in every mode; only the general subagent carries Lily's subtask prompt, replacing OpenCode's coding-CLI identity.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 integration audit: Lily's subtask prompt replaced explore's specialist prompt (whose lily_* tool hints do not even apply to it), and the shared edit/write ask — merged after the engine's explore rules — overrode their deny, so the host could approve an explore subagent's edits with nothing but a prompt line left to stop it, and that line had been replaced.
gates.failureFallback: Agent-level permission merges last in the engine, so the deny holds whatever the shared config says; explore's model pin and step budget are unchanged; general is unchanged. Mutation-verified: making explore editable again and giving it Lily's prompt each fail by name.

gates.protects: A turn that ended normally is judged a failure only by structure and provenance, never by what a correct answer looks like. A fragment is a failure when the stream ended without a recognized finish (unknown/length), began mid-sequence (leading whitespace then a lowercase word), carries a serialized source string (a statement end, a literal backslash-n, more code), closes a bold run it never opened, or echoes Lily's internal skill namespace the user never typed. A leaked tool call needs call structure outside code — two markers, call syntax with arguments, a marker opening a JSON argument object, or nothing but markup — and reasoning counts only when no tool ran and it ENDS in an unclosed call.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: MICRO_COMPLETION replayed complete short answers (391, 晴朗, 约4小时18分, Hello, world, Promise<string>) as failures because they had few tokens and no full stop; MALFORMED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT fired on answers explaining <invoke>/<parameter> in code fences, on a sentence naming <tool_call>, and on reasoning that merely discussed the format.
gates.failureFallback: The recorded field fragments (' file paths, and a single research question'; a leaked paragraphs.push(...)\\n blob; system-guide echoes; unpaired bold; the reasoning-only write call; DSML control tokens; multi-marker XML leaks) are still caught. Kill switch LILY_MICRO_COMPLETION_GUARD=0 unchanged. Mutation-verified: restoring the short-answer rule, dropping code stripping and scanning reasoning unconditionally each fail by name.

gates.protects: A delivered answer is never replaced by a template when anything was read. Evidence is everything the model was shown this turn (tool output plus pre-extracted document and image text), and the source-content fallback replaces an answer only on proof nothing was read: no source-content observation and no tool call whose input names the attachment. Every other gate failure keeps the answer and appends a note. A library request the host only GUESSED from wording gets the full authoring workflow worded conditionally and binds the persistence tool only once the model calls it; an explicit UI choice still requires it. A persistence failure leads the output and keeps the model's content below it.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: a fully read quote was replaced over an 'ungrounded' 52,800 元 because numeric grounding ignored pre-extracted text; an answer the model read with its own script after pre-extraction failed was replaced as 'not read'; '设计一个游戏角色的背景故事' and '做一个自动回复邮件的 agent 脚本' were forced into the Character Worlds / agent workflows and the answer replaced by '角色没有保存到角色库'.
gates.failureFallback: An attachment nothing touched is still replaced (fabrication by construction); an explicit authoring choice is still enforced. Mutation-verified: replacing on any failure, ignoring observed text, erasing on persistence failure, and a guessed intent binding unconditionally each fail by name.

gates.protects: The post-edit syntax check runs node --check only on plain JavaScript; valid TypeScript and JSX are never reported as syntax errors (the engine's LSP diagnoses those).
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: every edit of a valid .ts/.tsx/.jsx file returned '[verify] Syntax error … Fix this before continuing', pushing the model to 'fix' correct code.
gates.failureFallback: A real JS syntax error is still caught; JSON and Python checks unchanged. Mutation-verified: checking TS again fails by name.

gates.protects: A reply is stripped as an echoed internal handoff only when a handoff was in its context (compaction, context rebuild, short-follow-up, recovery or legacy hydration). A reply in the handoff template with no handoff in context is content the user asked for and is never held, stripped or dropped from a rebuilt conversation.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: a user-requested handoff document in the 'Goal / Constraints & Preferences / Progress / Relevant Files' shape was replaced by '该轮回复只输出了内部状态摘要…已隐藏' because detection read headers only.
gates.failureFallback: Unknown provenance keeps the previous behaviour; the recorded field echoes (after compaction/resume/short follow-up) are still stripped. Mutation-verified: treating every turn as carrying a handoff fails by name.

gates.protects: The unfinished-todo continuation never forces a guess: the prompt tells a model that needs the user's decision to stop and ask, the gate settles after two consecutive no-progress nudges, and the answer given before the continuation survives it, whichever way the turn settles.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: a model that asked the user '用哪个模板？' was pushed back up to twice more, guessing on the user's behalf; the continuation reply ('已全部标记完成') could replace the real answer given before it.
gates.failureFallback: A model making progress still earns nudges; two no-progress nudges is the field-measured bound (a second still completes items 7/16 times, later ones 7/23); the shared continuation budget and LILY_DISABLE_TODO_COMPLETION_GATE=1 are unchanged. Mutation-verified: no pre-gate capture and a changed nudge count each fail by name.

gates.protects: The external-fact gate does not fail correct answers on form: a time word alone does not make a question about the user's attached source an external fact; a number one arithmetic step from grounded numbers (difference, sum, product, ratio, percentage) is grounded; a ranked list is checked against the whole evidence, and an abbreviation of a name the evidence spells out goes to the semantic judge instead of being called fabricated.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: '目前这个合同里违约金是多少？' with the contract attached was replayed for missing web links; '¥2,000 / 33.3%' computed from two fetched prices was flagged invented; '上海交大' against '上海交通大学' failed the ranking and never reached the judge; rankings were matched against the first 500 chars of evidence only.
gates.failureFallback: A number no arithmetic on the evidence yields and an entry the evidence never names are still flagged; the same time word about the world still activates the gate; abbreviation windows only feed the judge (no judge = the previous fail-open delivery). Deferred, not changed: proactive research on a general question still requires a link before a first-pass repair, because repairing first would attach sources to a wrong answer. Mutation-verified: removing the attachment exemption, the derivation, the whole-evidence corpus and the abbreviation windows each fail by name.

gates.protects: A resumed engine session is discarded after a visible model/gateway failure only when a side-effecting tool was still IN FLIGHT when the failure hit (or a user card was pending); tools that completed are recorded in the session history, so the conversation is kept.
gates.baseline: 2026-09-28 audit: any side-effecting tool that ran during the turn marked the session unaccountable, so a gateway 504 after 50 completed edits cleared the resume id and the next 'continue' got a 12K lossy local rebuild.
gates.failureFallback: An in-flight side-effecting tool still drops the resume (the original safety reason); replay of a side-effecting turn is still refused separately. Mutation-verified: restoring 'ran any unsafe tool' fails by name.

gates.protects: Switching the model — by the user or by auto mode routing a turn to another chosen model — rebuilds the serve from the new config and keeps the engine session (recycle): an engine session is not bound to a model; every message records its own and every prompt names the model it runs on.

gates.protects: The enterprise back office works as a closed loop on both sides. Two-layer switch: organizations.status is derived by a DB CHECK from owner_status (the enterprise owner's own pause) and platform_status (the platform's freeze), so an enterprise can never lift a platform freeze and the platform cannot un-pause an owner's pause; every existing reader of status keeps its meaning. The identity the user picks pays: with x-lily-organization-id only the org pool is charged (per-request cap + a weekly member budget whose window starts at the first charge and resets 7 days later; member override > org default > unlimited), without it only the personal balance; a pool shortage is ORG_POOL_INSUFFICIENT. Admins cannot act on other admins/owners; the last owner cannot step down or leave; ownership transfers in one step; any member can leave (issued accounts excepted). Invitation phones are normalised to E.164 and expire; seats deferred while an org was disabled are granted when it becomes active. Removed issued accounts stay listed and are restored by re-adding. Every enterprise-side mutation writes its audit_logs row in the same transaction; both consoles read the org history. Platform grants are idempotent per form key and can be reduced/revoked with a ledger row. Org-pool grants (booked under the owner's user_id) never count as the owner's personal balance in admin users list/detail or the personal statement. Self-serve org creation is closed (ORG_CREATE_PLATFORM_ONLY). Every server enterprise code has a zh/en/ar message.

The admin PATCH still accepts the legacy {status} form (disabled = suspended). Unknown future codes still render a message naming the code. Mutation-verified against real Postgres: removing the peer guard, making the freeze owner-liftable, restoring personal-first billing, dropping the weekly gate, dropping the owner-balance filter, or dropping deferred redemption each fails the closed loop by name.
